q: Snowflake provides a mechanism for its customers to override its natural clustering algorithms. This method is:
e:
- Clustering keys: Snowflake permite a los usuarios definir 'Clustering keys' para anular manualmente su proceso natural de clustering. Esto ayuda a optimizar el rendimiento de las consultas al agrupar los datos de manera más eficiente en función de las columnas clave especificadas.
- Micro-partitions: Micro-partitions son unidades de almacenamiento automáticas en Snowflake, pero no son un mecanismo para controlar el clustering.
- Key partitions: Esta no es una característica de Snowflake; no utiliza key partitions para el clustering.
- Clustered partitions: Aunque suena similar a clustering keys, no es una funcionalidad reconocida de Snowflake y no permite el control manual del clustering.

q: Which of the following are valid Snowflake Virtual Warehouse Scaling Policies? (Choose two.)
e:
- Economy, Standard: Las políticas de escalado válidas para los Virtual Warehouses en Snowflake son 'Economy' y 'Standard'. Estas políticas permiten gestionar los recursos computacionales del warehouse, equilibrando el rendimiento y los costos. 'Economy' es una opción que reduce los costos en situaciones de menor demanda, mientras que 'Standard' es la política predeterminada que proporciona un balance general de recursos.
- Custom: No es una política de escalado válida en Snowflake.
- Optimized: Aunque suena como una opción válida, no es una política de escalado reconocida en Snowflake.

q: True or False: A single database can exist in more than one Snowflake account.
e: True. Snowflake supports database replication across multiple accounts, so the same database can exist as a primary database in one account and as secondary replica(s) in other account(s).

q: Which of the following roles is recommended to be used to create and manage users and roles?
e: The 'SECURITYADMIN' role is recommended for creating and managing users and roles in Snowflake. This role has the necessary privileges for user and role administration.

q: True or False: Bulk unloading of data from Snowflake supports the use of a SELECT statement.
e: It is true that bulk unloading of data from Snowflake supports the use of a SELECT statement. This feature allows for the specific selection of data during the unloading process.

q: Select the different types of Internal Stages: (Choose three.)
e: The different types of Internal Stages in Snowflake include 'Named Stage', 'User Stage', and 'Table Stage'. These stages are used for data loading and unloading purposes.

q: True or False: A customer using SnowSQL / native connectors will be unable to also use the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) unless access to the UI is explicitly granted by support.
e: This statement is false. Customers using SnowSQL or native connectors can also use the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) without needing explicit permission from support.

q: Account-level storage usage can be monitored via:
o: The Snowflake Web Interface (UI) in the Databases section
The Snowflake Web Interface (UI) in the Account -> Billing & Usage section
The Account Usage Schema -> ACCOUNT_USAGE_METRICS View
e: Account-level storage usage in Snowflake can be monitored via the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) in the 'Account -> Billing & Usage' section. This feature provides insights into storage consumption and associated costs.

q: Credit Consumption by the Compute Layer (Virtual Warehouses) is based on: (Choose two.)
o: The number of clusters for the Warehouse
e: Credit consumption by the Compute Layer in Snowflake, particularly for Virtual Warehouses, is primarily based on the size of the warehouse and the number of clusers for the Warehouse. The number of users and Amount of data processed are not direct factors in credit consumption. Another consideration is the length of time the compute resources in each cluster runs, although this is not covered in these factors.

q: Which statement best describes `clustering`?
o: Clustering represents the way data is grouped together and stored within Snowflake's micro-partitions
The database administrator must define the clustering methodology for each Snowflake table
The clustering key must be included on the COPY command when loading data into Snowflake
Clustering can be disabled within a Snowflake account
e: Clustering in Snowflake refers to how data is organized within micro-partitions. Snowflake automatically clusters data to optimize query performance, and users can influence this through clustering keys. The other options do not accurately describe Snowflake's clustering feature.

q: True or False: The COPY command must specify a File Format in order to execute.
e: It is not mandatory to specify a File Format in the COPY command in Snowflake. If no file format is specified, Snowflake uses the default file format settings.

q: Which of the following commands sets the Virtual Warehouse for a session?
e: The command 'USE WAREHOUSE <<warehouse name>>;' is used to set the Virtual Warehouse for a session in Snowflake. This command specifies which warehouse should be used for executing queries in the current session.

q: Which of the following objects can be cloned? (Choose four.)
e: In Snowflake, the objects that can be cloned include tables, schemas, databases, and named file formats. Shares and Users cannot be cloned. Cloning creates a zero-copy snapshot of the object at a specific point in time.

q: Which object allows you to limit the number of credits consumed within a Snowflake account?
e: The 'Resource Monitor' in Snowflake is the tool that allows account administrators to set limits on the number of credits consumed. It is used for monitoring and controlling the usage of compute resources to avoid unexpected expenses.

q: Snowflake is designed for which type of workloads? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake is specifically designed for OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) workloads and concurrent workloads, where it can handle multiple queries simultaneously without performance degradation. It is not optimized for OLTP (Online Transaction Processing) or on-premise workloads.

q: What are the three layers that make up Snowflake's architecture? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake's architecture consists of three layers: the Compute layer, the Storage layer, and the Cloud Services layer. These layers work together to provide a fully managed, scalable, and secure data platform.

q: Why would a customer size a Virtual Warehouse from an X-Small to a Medium?
o: To accommodate a more complex workload
e: Resizing a Virtual Warehouse (scaling up) from X-Small to Medium increases compute resources per cluster, which improves performance for larger, more complex queries. The Snowflake documentation explicitly states that 'warehouse resizing is not intended for handling concurrency issues; instead, use additional warehouses to handle the workload or use a multi-cluster warehouse.' For accommodating more concurrent queries or users, multi-cluster warehouses (scaling out) are the recommended approach.

q: True or False: Reader Accounts incur no additional Compute costs to the Data Provider since they are simply reading the shared data without making changes.
e: This statement is false. Reader accounts in Snowflake can incur additional compute costs to the data provider. While the reader accounts are used for accessing shared data, the compute resources used by these accounts can lead to additional costs.

q: Which of the following connectors allow Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) authorization when connecting? (Choose all that apply.)
e: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is supported by Snowflake for JDBC, SnowSQL, the Snowflake Web Interface (UI), Python and ODBC connectors. These methods enhance security by requiring multiple forms of verification when accessing Snowflake.

q: True or False: Snowflake charges a premium for storing semi-structured data.
e: Snowflake does not charge a premium for storing semi-structured data such as JSON, XML, or Avro. Snowflake's architecture allows it to handle semi-structured data efficiently without additional costs.

q: Which of the following statements describes a benefit of Snowflake's separation of compute and storage? (Choose all that apply.)
o: Growth of storage and compute are tightly coupled together
Storage expands without the requirement to add more compute
Compute can be scaled up or down without the requirement to add more storage
Multiple compute clusters can access stored data without contention
e: One of the key benefits of Snowflake's architecture is the separation of storage and compute. This separation allows for independent scaling of storage and compute resources and enables multiple compute clusters to access the same stored data without contention.

q: True or False: It is possible to unload structured data to semi-structured formats such as JSON and Parquet.
e: It is true that Snowflake supports unloading structured data into semi-structured formats like JSON and Parquet. This flexibility allows for a wide range of data interchange and integration scenarios.

q: In which layer of its architecture does Snowflake store its metadata statistics?
e: Snowflake stores its metadata statistics in the Cloud Services Layer. This layer acts as the brain of the Snowflake architecture, managing all aspects of data storage, optimization, and security.

q: True or False: Data in fail-safe can be deleted by a user or the Snowflake team before it expires.
e: It is false that data in fail-safe can be deleted before it expires. Fail-safe is an automatic feature in Snowflake that provides a 7-day window of data protection beyond the Time Travel period and cannot be manually altered.

q: True or False: Snowflake's data warehouse was built from the ground up for the cloud in lieu of using an existing database or a platform, like Hadoop, as a base.
e: It is true that Snowflake's data warehouse was built from the ground up specifically for the cloud. It was not based on an existing database or platform like Hadoop, but rather designed to leverage the full capabilities and advantages of cloud computing.

q: Which of the following statements are true of Virtual Warehouses? (Choose all that apply.)
o: Customers can change the size of the Warehouse after creation
A Warehouse can be resized while running
A Warehouse can be configured to suspend after a period of inactivity
A Warehouse can be configured to auto-resume when new queries are submitted
e: All the provided statements are true of Virtual Warehouses in Snowflake. Customers have the flexibility to change the warehouse size, resize it while it's running, and configure it to suspend after inactivity and auto-resume for new queries, optimizing both performance and cost.

q: The PUT command: (Choose two.)
o: Automatically creates a File Format object
Automatically uses the last Stage created
e: The PUT command in Snowflake automatically compresses files using Gzip and encrypts them using AES-256 for secure transfer to Snowflake-managed storage (internal stages). It does not automatically create a File Format object nor use the last stage created unless explicitly specified.

q: Which type of table corresponds to a single Snowflake session?
e: Temporary tables in Snowflake are session-specific. They exist only during the life of the session that created them, and they are automatically dropped at the end of the session.

q: Which interfaces can be used to create and/or manage Virtual Warehouses?
e: Virtual Warehouses in Snowflake can be created and managed using the Snowflake Web Interface (UI), SQL commands, and data integration tools. All these interfaces provide mechanisms for warehouse management.

q: When a Pipe is recreated using the CREATE OR REPLACE PIPE command:
o: The Pipe load history is reset to empty
The REFRESH parameter is set to TRUE
Previously loaded files will be ignored
e:
- The Pipe load history is reset to empty: Al recrear un Pipe usando el comando CREATE OR REPLACE PIPE, el historial de carga del Pipe se reinicia. Esto significa que Snowflake ya no tendrá un registro de los archivos que fueron procesados previamente por ese Pipe.
- The REFRESH parameter is set to TRUE: El parámetro REFRESH es parte del comando ALTER PIPE, no del comando CREATE OR REPLACE PIPE.
- Previously loaded files will be ignored: Al recrear un Pipe, los archivos previamente cargados pueden ser procesados de nuevo si se ejecuta el comando ALTER PIPE ... REFRESH.
- All of the above: No todos los elementos mencionados son correctos; solamente la opción A es la respuesta correcta.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition that customers planning on storing protected information in Snowflake should consider for regulatory compliance?
e: For customers needing to store protected information in Snowflake, the Business Critical Edition (or higher) is recommended for regulatory compliance. This edition offers enhanced security features such as end-to-end encryption and additional compliance certifications.

q: Select the three types of tables that exist within Snowflake. (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake supports three main types of tables: Temporary, Transient, and Permanent. Each type serves different use cases and has unique characteristics in terms of data persistence and performance.

q: True or False: Snowpipe via REST API can only reference External Stages as source.
e: Snowpipe via REST API in Snowflake can reference both internal and external stages as sources for data loading. This allows for greater flexibility in data integration from various sources.

q: True or False: A third-party tool that supports standard JDBC or ODBC but has no Snowflake-specific driver will be unable to connect to Snowflake.
e: A third-party tool that supports standard JDBC or ODBC protocols can connect to Snowflake, even if it does not have a Snowflake-specific driver. Snowflake provides JDBC and ODBC drivers to facilitate these connections.

q: True or False: It is possible to load data into Snowflake without creating a named File Format object.
e: It is true that data can be loaded into Snowflake without creating a named File Format object. Snowflake allows users to specify file format options directly in the COPY INTO command, eliminating the need for a separate File Format object.

q: True or False: A table in Snowflake can only be queried using the Virtual Warehouse that was used to load the data.
e: This statement is false. In Snowflake, a table can be queried using any Virtual Warehouse, not just the one that was used to load the data. This flexibility is a part of Snowflake's architecture, where storage and compute are separate.

q: Which of the following statements are true of Snowflake data loading? (Choose three.)
o: VARIANT ‘null’ values are not the same as SQL NULL values
It is recommended to do frequent, single row DMLs
It is recommended to validate the data before loading into the Snowflake target table
It is recommended to use staging tables to manage MERGE statements
e: In Snowflake, VARIANT 'null' values are different from SQL NULL values. Validating data before loading and using staging tables for managing MERGE statements are recommended practices for efficient and accurate data loading.

q: Which statements are true of micro-partitions? (Choose two.)
o: They are stored compressed only if COMPRESS=TRUE on Table
They are only encrypted in the Enterprise edition and above
e: Micro-partitions in Snowflake are approximately 16MB in size and are immutable, meaning once written, they cannot be modified. This immutability is a key aspect of Snowflake's architecture. Encryption of micro-partitions is standard across all editions of Snowflake, not just the Enterprise edition.

q: True or False: Query ID's are unique across all Snowflake deployments and can be used in communication with Snowflake Support to help troubleshoot issues.
e: Query IDs in Snowflake are unique across all deployments. They are a valuable tool for identifying specific queries, especially when communicating with Snowflake Support to troubleshoot issues.

q: A deterministic query is run at 8am, takes 5 minutes, and the results are cached. Which of the following statements are true? (Choose two.)
o: The exact query will ALWAYS return the precomputed result set for the RESULT_CACHE_ACTIVE = time period
The same exact query will return the precomputed results if the underlying data hasn't changed and the results were last accessed within previous 24 hour period
The same exact query will return the precomputed results even if the underlying data has changed as long as the results were last accessed within the previous 24 hour period
The €24ג hourג€ timer on the precomputed results gets renewed every time the exact query is executed
e: Snowflake caches the results of deterministic queries. These cached results are reused if the same query is executed again, provided the underlying data has not changed and the cache is still active, typically within a 24-hour period. The cache timer is reset every time the query is executed.

q: Increasing the maximum number of clusters in a Multi-Cluster Warehouse is an example of:
e: Increasing the maximum number of clusters in a Multi-Cluster Warehouse in Snowflake is an example of 'scaling out'. This involves adding more clusters to handle larger loads, rather than increasing the resources (like CPU or memory) of existing clusters, which would be 'scaling up'.

q: Which statement best describes Snowflake tables?
o: Snowflake tables are logical representations of underlying physical data
Snowflake tables are the physical instantiation of data loaded into Snowflake
Snowflake tables require that clustering keys be defined to perform optimally
Snowflake tables are owned by a user
e: Snowflake tables are best described as logical representations of the underlying physical data. They provide a structured view of the data, but do not represent the physical storage of data in Snowflake, which is handled differently to optimize performance and storage efficiency.

q: Which item in the Data Warehouse migration process does not apply in Snowflake?
e: In Snowflake, migrating indexes is not applicable because Snowflake does not use traditional database indexes. Snowflake's architecture automatically optimizes data storage and query performance without the need for manual index maintenance.

q: Snowflake provides two mechanisms to reduce data storage costs for short-lived tables. These mechanisms are: (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake offers Temporary and Transient Tables as mechanisms to reduce data storage costs, especially for short-lived data. Temporary Tables are session-specific and deleted after the session ends, while Transient Tables have a longer life but do not support Time Travel and Fail-safe, thus reducing storage costs.

q: What is the maximum compressed row size in Snowflake?
e: The maximum compressed row size in Snowflake is 16MB. This size limitation is related to the maximum size of micro-partitions, which are the fundamental storage units in Snowflake's architecture.

q: Which of the following are main sections of the top navigation of the Snowflake Web Interface (UI)? (Choose three.)
e: The main sections of the top navigation of the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) include 'Databases', 'Warehouses', and 'Worksheets'. These sections provide easy access to the respective features and functionalities within the Snowflake environment.

q: What is the recommended Snowflake data type to store semi-structured data like JSON?
e: The VARIANT data type in Snowflake is specifically designed to store semi-structured data like JSON, XML, and Avro. It can store values up to a maximum size of 16 MB and is ideal for handling flexible schemas inherent in semi-structured data.

q: Which of the following statements are true of Snowflake releases: (Choose two.)
o: They roll up and release approximately monthly, but customers can request early release application
During a release, new customer requests/queries/connections transparently move over to the newer version
A customer is assigned a 30 minute window (that can be moved anytime within a week) during which the system will be unavailable and customer is upgraded
e: Snowflake's releases happen approximately weekly and During a release, new customer requests/queries/connections transparently move over to the newer version.

q: Which of the following are common use cases for zero-copy cloning? (Choose three.)
o: Quick provisioning of Dev and Test/QA environments
e: Zero-copy cloning in Snowflake is commonly used for quickly provisioning development and test/QA environments, creating data backups, and taking point-in-time snapshots. This feature allows for the creation of full data set clones almost instantly without duplicating the physical storage, thereby saving time and resources.

q: If a Small Warehouse is made up of 2 servers/cluster, how many servers/cluster make up a Medium Warehouse?
e: In Snowflake, the size of a Virtual Warehouse is determined by the number of servers per cluster. A Small Warehouse comprises 2 servers per cluster, and the size doubles with each increment. Therefore, a Medium Warehouse consists of 4 servers per cluster.

q: True or False: When a data share is established between a Data Provider and a Data Consumer, the Data Consumer can extend that data share to other Data Consumers.
e: It is false that a Data Consumer can extend a data share to other Data Consumers. In Snowflake, only the Data Provider has the ability to share data. Data Consumers cannot re-share the data they receive with other accounts.

q: Which is true of Snowflake network policies? A Snowflake network policy: (Choose two.)
o: Is available to all Snowflake Editions
Is only available to customers with Business Critical Edition
Restricts or enables access to specific IP addresses
Is activated using an ‘ALTER DATABASE’ command
e: Snowflake network policies, which are available to all Snowflake Editions, allow administrators to restrict or enable access to specific IP addresses, enhancing the security of the Snowflake environment.

q: True or False: Snowflake charges additional fees to Data Providers for each Share they create.
e: It is false that Snowflake charges additional fees to Data Providers for each Share they create. Snowflake does not charge for creating and maintaining data shares. However, costs can be incurred for the compute resources used by Data Consumers when accessing shared data.

q: Query results are stored in the Result Cache for how long after they are last accessed, assuming no data changes have occurred?
e: In Snowflake, query results are stored in the Result Cache for 24 hours after they are last accessed, assuming no changes have occurred to the underlying data. This feature improves performance by reusing the results of previous queries.

q: A role is created and owns 2 tables. This role is then dropped. Who will now own the two tables?
o: The user that deleted the role
The assumed role that dropped the role
e: When a role that owns objects such as tables is dropped in Snowflake, the ownership of these objects is automatically transferred to role that dropped the role. This prevents the objects from becoming orphaned and ensures that they remain manageable within the system.

q: Which of the following connectors are available in the Downloads section of the Snowflake Web Interface (UI)? (Choose two.)
e: In the Downloads section of the Snowflake Web Interface, users can find connectors for SnowSQL and ODBC. These connectors enable users to connect to and interact with Snowflake using various client applications and programming languages.

q: Which of the following DML commands isn't supported by Snowflake?
e: Snowflake does not support the UPSERT DML command. However, it does support MERGE, UPDATE, and TRUNCATE TABLE commands. The MERGE command in Snowflake can be used to achieve similar functionality as UPSERT in other database systems.

q: Which of the following statements is true of zero-copy cloning?
o: Zero-copy clones increase storage costs as cloning the table requires storing its data twice
All zero-copy clone objects inherit the privileges of their original objects
Zero-copy cloning is licensed as an additional Snowflake feature
At the instance/instant a clone is created, all micro-partitions in the original table and the clone are fully shared
e: Zero-copy cloning in Snowflake creates a clone of a table or database without duplicating the underlying data. At the time of cloning, all micro-partitions are fully shared between the original and the clone, thus not increasing storage costs. This feature leverages Snowflake's unique architecture to provide efficient data duplication.

q: True or False: When a user creates a role, they are initially assigned ownership of the role and they maintain ownership until it is transferred to another user.
e: In Snowflake, when a user creates a role, they are initially assigned the CREATE_ROLE privilege on the role. However, they do not automatically become the owner of the role. The ownership of the role is initially set to the SYSADMIN role.

q: The Query History in the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) is kept for approximately:
e: Query History page available under Activity menu on Web UI, holds query data for 14 days. And you can Query_history view available in Account_Usage schema holds query data for 365 days

q: To run a Multi-Cluster Warehouse in auto-scale mode, a user would:
o: Configure the Maximum Clusters setting to ‘Auto-Scale’
Set the Minimum Clusters and Maximum Clusters settings to the same value
Set the Minimum Clusters and Maximum Clusters settings to the different values
e: To enable auto-scaling in a Multi-Cluster Warehouse, a user must set the Minimum Clusters and Maximum Clusters settings to different values. This configuration allows the warehouse to automatically scale out or in based on the workload.

q: Which of the following terms best describes Snowflake's database architecture?
e: Snowflake's database architecture is best described as 'Multi-cluster, shared data'. This architecture allows multiple compute clusters to operate on the same set of data, enabling high performance and concurrency.

q: Which of the following are options when creating a Virtual Warehouse? (Choose two.)
e: When creating a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake, the options include 'Auto-resume' and 'Auto-suspend'. These features allow the warehouse to automatically resume operations when queries are submitted and suspend after a period of inactivity, optimizing resource usage and cost.

q: A Virtual Warehouse's auto-suspend and auto-resume settings apply to:
o: The primary cluster in the Virtual Warehouse
The database the Virtual Warehouse resides in
The queries currently being run by the Virtual Warehouse
e: Auto-suspend and auto-resume settings in Snowflake apply to the entire Virtual Warehouse, not just the primary cluster or the specific queries. These settings help manage warehouse resources efficiently by automatically suspending the warehouse when it's idle and resuming it when needed.

q: Fail-safe is unavailable on which table types? (Choose two.)
e: Fail-safe, a feature in Snowflake for data recovery, is not available for Temporary and Transient tables. Fail-safe provides an additional layer of protection by retaining historical data for a period after the Time Travel retention period ends, but it doesn't apply to these two types of tables.

q: Which of the following objects is not covered by Time Travel?
e: In Snowflake, Time Travel allows users to access historical data within a specified retention period, but it does not cover 'Stages'. Time Travel applies to objects like Tables, Schemas, and Databases, enabling point-in-time recovery and data analysis.

q: True or False: Micro-partition metadata enables some operations to be completed without requiring Compute.
e: True. Micro-partition metadata in Snowflake enables certain operations to be completed without the need for active compute resources. This metadata, which includes information about the data stored in micro-partitions, allows Snowflake to perform operations like pruning during query execution efficiently.

q: Which of the following commands are not blocking operations? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, both 'INSERT' and 'COPY' commands are typically non-blocking operations. They can be executed concurrently with other transactions, unlike 'UPDATE' and 'MERGE' commands, which may require locks on the tables and can block other operations.

q: Which of the following is true of Snowpipe via REST API? (Choose two.)
o: You can only use it on Internal Stages
All COPY INTO options are available during pipe creation
Snowflake automatically manages the compute required to execute the Pipe's COPY INTO commands
Snowpipe keeps track of which files it has loaded
e: When using Snowpipe via REST API, Snowflake automatically manages the compute resources required for the Pipe's COPY INTO commands. Additionally, Snowpipe tracks which files have been loaded, preventing duplicate loading.

q: Snowflake recommends, as a minimum, that all users with the following role(s) should be enrolled in Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA):
e: Snowflake strongly recommends requiring MFA for users with the ACCOUNTADMIN role. The documentation states that this recommendation applies particularly to ACCOUNTADMIN users, and can also be expanded to users with the SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN roles.

q: When can a Virtual Warehouse start running queries?
o: Only during administrator defined time slots
e: A Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake can start running queries as soon as its provisioning is complete. Provisioning includes the allocation of compute resources, after which the warehouse is ready to execute queries.

q: True or False: Users are able to see the result sets of queries executed by other users that share their same role.
e: It is false that users can see the result sets of queries executed by other users sharing the same role. In Snowflake, query results are specific to the user session and are not shared across different users, even if they have the same role.

q: True or False: The user has to specify which cluster a query will run on in a multi-cluster Warehouse.
e: It is false that users need to specify which cluster a query will run on in a multi-cluster Warehouse. In Snowflake, the system automatically manages query distribution across clusters within a multi-cluster warehouse.

q: True or False: Pipes can be suspended and resumed.
e: True. In Snowflake, Pipes, which are used for continuous data loading, can indeed be suspended and later resumed. This feature allows for better control and management of data loading processes, especially in cases where data loading needs to be temporarily halted for maintenance or cost management.

q: Which of the following languages can be used to implement Snowflake User Defined Functions (UDFs)? (Choose three.)
e: In Snowflake, User Defined Functions (UDFs) can be implemented using Javascript,SQL and Python. These languages provide the necessary flexibility and capability for creating custom functions to handle various data processing and transformation tasks within Snowflake.

q: When should you consider disabling auto-suspend for a Virtual Warehouse? (Choose two.)
o: When users will be using compute at different times throughout a 24/7 period
When the compute must be available with no delay or lag time
When you do not want to have to manually turn on the Warehouse each time a user needs it
e: Disabling auto-suspend for a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake is advisable when immediate compute availability is critical (i.e., no delay or lag time is acceptable) and when consistent accessibility is needed without the need for manual intervention to resume the warehouse.

q: Which of the following are valid approaches to loading data into a Snowflake table? (Choose all that apply.)
o: Bulk copy from an External Stage
Continuous load using Snowpipe REST API
The Snowflake Web Interface (UI) data loading wizard
Bulk copy from an Internal Stage
e: Snowflake supports a variety of data loading methods, including bulk copying from both external and internal stages, using the Snowpipe REST API for continuous loading, and utilizing the Snowflake Web Interface's data loading wizard. These methods offer flexibility in handling different data loading requirements.

q: If auto-suspend is enabled for a Virtual Warehouse, the Warehouse is automatically suspended when:
o: All Snowflakes sessions using the Warehouse are terminated.
The last query using the Warehouse completes.
There are no users logged into Snowflake.
The Warehouse is inactive for a specified period of time.
e: If auto-suspend is enabled for a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake, the warehouse will automatically suspend itself after being inactive for a user-defined period of time. This period is configurable and helps in optimizing resource usage and cost.

q: True or False: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) in Snowflake is only supported in conjunction with Single Sign-On (SSO).
e: It is false that Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) in Snowflake is only supported in conjunction with Single Sign-On (SSO). MFA in Snowflake can be used independently of SSO, providing an additional layer of security for user authentication.

q: The number of queries that a Virtual Warehouse can concurrently process is determined by (Choose two.):
o: The CONCURRENT_QUERY_LIMIT parameter set on the Snowflake account
The size of the data required for each query
The tool that is executing the query
e: Snowflake documentation states that the number of queries a warehouse can concurrently process is determined by the size and complexity of each query. So the best choices are the complexity option and the size-related option. The docs do not mention CONCURRENT_QUERY_LIMIT; the documented concurrency-related parameter is MAX_CONCURRENCY_LEVEL.

q: Which of the following statements are true of VALIDATION_MODE in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: The VALIDATION_MODE option is used when creating an Internal Stage
VALIDATION_MODE=RETURN_ALL_ERRORS is a parameter of the COPY command
The VALIDATION_MODE option will validate data to be loaded by the COPY statement while completing the load and will return the rows that could not be loaded without error
The VALIDATION_MODE option will validate data to be loaded by the COPY statement without completing the load and will return possible errors
e: VALIDATION_MODE is a parameter of the COPY command, which can be set to RETURN_ALL_ERRORS to validate data without completing the load. This option allows Snowflake to return potential errors, helping users to identify and fix data issues before the load is finalized.

q: What privileges are required to create a task?
o: The GLOBAL privilege CREATE TASK is required to create a new task.
Tasks are created at the Application level and can only be created by the Account Admin role.
Many Snowflake DDLs are metadata operations only, and CREATE TASK DDL can be executed without virtual warehouse requirement or task specific grants.
The role must have access to the target schema and the CREATE TASK privilege on the schema itself.
e: To create a task in Snowflake, the role must have access to the target schema and possess the CREATE TASK privilege on that schema. This ensures that only authorized users can set up and manage tasks within a specific schema.

q: What are the three things customers want most from their enterprise data warehouse solution? (Choose three.)
e: Customers typically seek simplicity, concurrency, and performance in their enterprise data warehouse solutions. They desire an easy-to-use platform that can handle multiple concurrent queries efficiently and deliver high performance.

q: True or False: Some queries can be answered through the metadata cache and do not require an active Virtual Warehouse.
e: True. In Snowflake, certain queries can be answered directly from the metadata cache, which contains information about the structure and contents of the stored data. This means that these queries do not require an active Virtual Warehouse, thus saving on compute resources.

q: When scaling out by adding clusters to a multi-cluster warehouse, you are primarily scaling for improved:
e: When you scale out a multi-cluster warehouse in Snowflake by adding more clusters, the primary goal is to improve concurrency. This means enabling more queries to be run simultaneously without degradation in performance.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition that provides data sharing?
e: The minimum Snowflake edition that provides data sharing capabilities is the Standard edition. This allows organizations to share data across different Snowflake accounts, facilitating collaboration and data exchange.

q: True or False: Each worksheet in the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) can be associated with different roles, databases, schemas, and Virtual Warehouses.
e: True. In the Snowflake Web Interface, each worksheet can be associated with different roles, databases, schemas, and Virtual Warehouses. This allows for a flexible and customizable environment where different contexts can be set for different worksheets.

q: True or False: You can query the files in an External Stage directly without having to load the data into a table.
e: True. In Snowflake, it is possible to query files stored in an External Stage directly, without the need to first load the data into a table. This feature allows users to perform queries on external data sets efficiently.

q: The FLATTEN function is used to query which type of data in Snowflake?
e: FLATTEN can be used with semi-structured data and also with structured ARRAY, OBJECT, and MAP values in Snowflake, so "Both of the above" is the best answer.

q: True or False: An active warehouse is required to run a COPY INTO statement.
e: It is true that an active warehouse is required to run a COPY INTO statement in Snowflake. The COPY INTO command requires compute resources, provided by a running virtual warehouse, to execute.

q: True or False: AWS Private Link provides a secure connection from the Customer's on-premise data center to the Snowflake.
e: It is true that AWS Private Link provides a secure connection from a customer's on-premise data center to Snowflake. This service enables private connectivity between AWS VPCs and Snowflake, enhancing security and data privacy.

q: True or False: Snowflake's Global Services Layer gathers and maintains statistics on all columns in all micro-partitions.
e: It is true that Snowflake's Global Services Layer gathers and maintains statistics on all columns in all micro-partitions. This layer is responsible for metadata management and optimization, among other functions.

q: True or False: It is best practice to define a clustering key on every table.
e: It is false that defining a clustering key on every table is a best practice in Snowflake. While clustering keys can improve performance on large tables, they are not always necessary and can be counterproductive on smaller tables.

q: Which of the following statements is true of Snowflake?
o: It was built specifically for the cloud
It was built as an on-premises solution and then ported to the cloud
It was designed as a hybrid database to allow customers to store data either on premises or in the cloud
It was built for Hadoop architecture
It's based on an Oracle Architecture
e: Snowflake was built specifically for the cloud, leveraging cloud architecture to provide scalability, flexibility, and cost-effective data storage and analytics. It was not an on-premises solution ported to the cloud, nor was it designed for Hadoop or based on Oracle architecture.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition that provides multi-cluster warehouses and up to 90 days of Time Travel?
e: The Enterprise edition of Snowflake provides the capabilities of multi-cluster warehouses and up to 90 days of Time Travel. This edition offers advanced features needed for larger-scale, more complex, and mission-critical operations.

q: How many shares can be consumed by a single Data Consumer?
o: 100, but can be increased by contacting support
e: A single Data Consumer in Snowflake can consume an unlimited number of shares. This flexibility allows organizations to access and analyze data from multiple sources without restrictions on the number of shares they can use.

q: What is the lowest Snowflake edition that offers Time Travel up to 90 days?
e: The Enterprise Edition of Snowflake is the lowest edition that offers the Time Travel feature for up to 90 days. This feature allows users to access historical data over an extended period, providing significant flexibility for data recovery and analysis.

q: Which of the following statements are true about Schemas in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: A Schema may contain one or more Databases
A Database may contain one or more Schemas
A Schema is a logical grouping of Database Objects
Each Schema is contained within a Warehouse
e: In Snowflake, a Schema is a logical grouping of database objects like tables, views, and functions, and each database can contain one or more schemas. However, a schema does not contain databases, nor is it contained within a warehouse.

q: True or False: You can resize a Virtual Warehouse while queries are running.
e: It is true that you can resize a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake while queries are running. Snowflake allows on-the-fly resizing of warehouses to scale compute resources up or down without interrupting running queries.

q: What is the most granular object that the Time Travel retention period can be defined on?
e: The most granular object that the Time Travel retention period can be defined on in Snowflake is a 'Table'. Time Travel settings can be specified at the table level, allowing for fine-grained control over data retention.

q: Which of the following statements is true of Snowflake micro-partitioning?
o: Micro-partitioning has been known to introduce data skew
Micro-partitioning: requires a partitioning schema to be defined up front
Micro-partitioning is transparently completed using the ordering that occurs when the data is inserted/loaded
Micro-partitioning can be disabled within a Snowflake account
e: Snowflake's micro-partitioning is transparently completed based on the order in which data is inserted or loaded. This automatic process optimizes data storage and query performance without requiring a predefined partitioning schema.

q: True or False: Snowflake bills for a minimum of five minutes each time a Virtual Warehouse is started.
e: It is False Because Snowflake utilizes per-second billing (with a 60-second minimum each time the warehouse starts), warehouses are billed only for the credits they actually consume when they are actively working.

q: When scaling up Virtual Warehouses by increasing Virtual Warehouse t-shirt size, you are primarily scaling for improved:
e: When scaling up Virtual Warehouses by increasing their size (e.g., from X-Small to Large), the primary goal is to improve performance. Larger warehouse sizes offer more compute resources, leading to faster query execution.

q: As a best practice, clustering keys should only be defined on tables of which minimum size?
e: As a best practice in Snowflake, clustering keys should generally be defined on tables that are in the multi-terabyte (TB) range. For smaller tables, the benefits of clustering may not be significant enough to justify the overhead.

q: How are Snowpipe charges calculated?
e: Snowpipe charges in Snowflake are calculated based on a per-second, per-core granularity. This means that charges are incurred based on the amount of compute resources utilized and the time those resources are used.

q: True or False: A Snowflake account is charged for data stored in both Internal and External Stages.
e: False. In Snowflake, while there are storage charges for data stored in Internal Stages, there are no storage charges for data in External Stages. External Stages refer to cloud storage locations outside of Snowflake, like Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage.

q: True or False: When active, a Pipe requires a dedicated Virtual Warehouse to execute.
e: False. A Snowpipe in Snowflake does not require a dedicated Virtual Warehouse to execute. Snowpipe automatically provisions and manages the compute resources required for loading data, separate from Virtual Warehouses.

q: True or False: Snowflake supports federated authentication in all editions.
e: True. Snowflake supports federated authentication across all of its editions. Federated authentication allows users to leverage their existing identity provider to authenticate with Snowflake, enhancing security and simplifying user management.

q: True or False: When a new Snowflake object is created, it is automatically owned by the user who created it.
e: False. When a new Snowflake object is created, it is automatically owned by the active primary ROLE of the session, not by the user. The OWNERSHIP privilege is granted to the role used to create the object. Users interact with the object through that role. This is a core principle of Snowflake's Discretionary Access Control (DAC) model.

q: True or False: A Virtual Warehouse consumes Snowflake credits even when inactive.
e: It is false that a Virtual Warehouse consumes Snowflake credits when inactive. Snowflake credits are only consumed when the warehouse is active and performing queries or other compute operations.

q: True or False: During data unloading, only JSON and CSV files can be compressed.
e: It is false that only JSON and CSV files can be compressed during data unloading in Snowflake. Snowflake supports compression for various file formats, not limited to JSON and CSV, when unloading data.

q: Which of the following are options when creating a Virtual Warehouse? (Choose two.)
e: When creating a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake, 'Auto-suspend' and 'Auto-resume' are two key options. They allow the warehouse to automatically suspend after a period of inactivity and resume when queries are submitted, optimizing resource usage and cost.

q: Which formats are supported for unloading data from Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake supports unloading data in Delimited formats (like CSV, TSV) for structured data and JSON for semi-structured data.

q: True or False: Data Providers can share data with only the Data Consumer.
e: False. In Snowflake, Data Providers can share data with Data Consumers and Data Readers. Data readers are users who have Reader accounts without requiring to become a Snowflake customer.

q: The fail-safe retention period is how many days?
e: The fail-safe retention period in Snowflake is 7 days. Fail-safe is an additional layer of data protection that provides a 7-day window to recover data after the Time Travel period has expired.

q: True or False: Once created, a micro-partition will never be changed.
e: True. In Snowflake, all data is stored in micro-partitions, which are contiguous units of storage that are immutable.

q: What services does Snowflake automatically provide for customers that they may have been responsible for with their on-premise system? (Choose all that apply.)
e: In a cloud-based system like Snowflake, services such as patching software, and maintaining metadata and statistics are automatically handled by the platform. Customers do not need to install and configure hardware as it is a cloud service.

q: Which of the following statements would be used to export/unload data from Snowflake?
e: The correct statement to export or unload data from Snowflake is 'COPY INTO @stage'. This command allows for data to be copied from Snowflake tables to stages (external storage locations), facilitating data export.

q: True or False: A 4X-Large Warehouse may, at times, take longer to provision than a X-Small Warehouse.
e: It is true that a 4X-Large Warehouse might take longer to provision than a X-Small Warehouse in Snowflake, because larger is not necessarily faster for smaller and more basic queries.

q: How would you determine the size of the virtual warehouse used for a task?
o: Root task may be executed concurrently (i.e., multiple instances), it is recommended to leave some margins in the execution window to avoid missing instances of execution
Querying (SELECT) the size of the stream content would help determine the warehouse size. For example, if querying large stream content, use a larger warehouse size
If using the stored procedure to execute multiple SQL statements, it's best to test run the stored procedure separately to size the compute resource first

Since task infrastructure is based on running the task body on schedule, it's recommended to configure the virtual warehouse for automatic concurrency handling using Multi-cluster warehouse (MCW) to match the task schedule
e: To determine the right warehouse size, Snowflake recommends starting with the task and workload, then comparing performance across multiple warehouse sizes. For task bodies that use stored procedures, testing the procedure separately is the closest available way to estimate the compute resources required. More generally, the documentation advises analyzing average task run times using different warehouses and clustering to choose an appropriate size.

q: The Information Schema and Account Usage Share provide storage information for which of the following objects? (Choose three.)
e: The Information Schema and Account Usage Share in Snowflake provide storage information for objects like Tables, Databases, and Internal Stages. These tools offer insights into the storage usage of these objects within Snowflake.

q: What is the default File Format used in the COPY command if one is not specified?
e: If no specific file format is defined in the COPY command in Snowflake, the default file format used is CSV. This is a commonly used format for data exchange and is the default setting for data loading operations.

q: True or False: Reader Accounts are able to extract data from shared data objects for use outside of Snowflake.
e: It is true that Reader Accounts are able to extract data from shared data objects for use outside of Snowflake. They can use the COPY INTO <location> command with their connection credentials to unload data into a cloud storage location.

q: True or False: You can define multiple columns within a clustering key on a table.
e: True. In Snowflake, it is possible to define a clustering key on a table that includes multiple columns. This allows for more complex clustering strategies that can improve query performance on large tables.

q: True or False: Snowflake enforces unique, primary key, and foreign key constraints during DML operations.
e: False. Snowflake does not enforce unique, primary key, and foreign key constraints during DML (Data Manipulation Language) operations. While these constraints can be defined for documentation and compatibility purposes, they are not enforced by Snowflake. Only NOT NULL constraints are always enforced.

q: True or False: Loading data into Snowflake requires that source data files be no larger than 16MB.
e: False. Snowflake does not have a strict size limit of 16MB for source data files when loading data. Larger files can be loaded, but for efficiency, it's often recommended to break them into smaller chunks.

q: True or False: A Virtual Warehouse can be resized while suspended.
e: True. A Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake can be resized even when it is suspended. This feature provides flexibility in managing the warehouse size according to varying workloads without the need for the warehouse to be active.

q: True or False: When you create a custom role, it is a best practice to immediately grant that role to ACCOUNTADMIN.
e: False. The custom role must be granted to the ACCOUNTADMIN role directly or, preferably, to another role in a hierarchy with the SYSADMIN role as the parent.

q: Which of the following accurately represents how a table fits into Snowflake's logical container hierarchy?
e: In Snowflake, the logical container hierarchy for a table is: Account -> Database -> Schema -> Table. This hierarchy starts with the account, under which multiple databases can exist. Each database can have multiple schemas, and under each schema, there can be multiple tables.

q: True or False: All Snowflake table types include fail-safe storage.
e: Not all Snowflake table types include fail-safe storage. Fail-safe is a data protection feature that provides a seven-day immutable storage layer beyond the Time Travel retention period. However, it is not applicable to all table types, such as temporary tables and transient tables.

q: What are two ways to create and manage Data Shares in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: Data Shares in Snowflake can be created and managed via the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) and through SQL commands. These methods provide the necessary functionality to establish and control data sharing between different Snowflake accounts.

q: True or False: Fail-safe can be disabled within a Snowflake account.
e: It is false that Fail-safe can be disabled within a Snowflake account. Fail-safe is a non-configurable, built-in feature in Snowflake that provides a 7-day data recovery window beyond the Time Travel retention period for protection against accidental data loss.

q: True or False: It is possible for a user to run a query against the query result cache without requiring an active Warehouse.
e: It is true that a user can run a query against the query result cache in Snowflake without requiring an active Warehouse. If the results of a previous query are available in the cache, Snowflake can return these results without needing to re-run the query on an active warehouse.

q: True or False: When Snowflake is configured to use Single Sign-On (SSO), Snowflake receives the usernames and credentials from the SSO service and loads them into the customer's Snowflake account.
e: False. When configured for Single Sign-On (SSO), Snowflake does not receive or load usernames and credentials from the SSO service into the Snowflake account. Instead, authentication is managed by the SSO service, and Snowflake relies on assertions provided by the SSO service to authenticate users.

q: Which of the following are best practices for loading data into Snowflake? (Choose three.)
o: Aim to produce data files that are between 100 MB and 250 MB in size, compressed.
Load data from files in a cloud storage service in a different region or cloud platform from the service or region containing the Snowflake account, to save on cost.
Enclose fields that contain delimiter characters in single or double quotes.
Split large files into a greater number of smaller files to distribute the load among the compute resources in an active warehouse.
When planning which warehouse(s) to use for data loading, start with the largest warehouse possible.
Partition the staged data into large folders with random paths, allowing Snowflake to determine the best way to load each file.
e: Best practices for loading data into Snowflake include producing data files of optimal size (100-250 MB compressed), properly enclosing fields with delimiter characters, and splitting larger files into smaller ones to efficiently distribute the load across compute resources.

q: Which Snowflake feature is used for both querying and restoring data?
e: Time Travel is a Snowflake feature that is used for both querying historical data and restoring data to a previous state. It allows users to access and revert data to earlier versions within a specified retention period.

q: What do the terms scale up and scale out refer to in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: Scaling out adds clusters of the same size to a virtual warehouse to handle more concurrent queries.
Scaling out adds clusters of varying sizes to a virtual warehouse.
Scaling out adds additional database servers to an existing running cluster to handle more concurrent queries.
Snowflake recommends using both scaling up and scaling out to handle more concurrent queries.
Scaling up resizes a virtual warehouse so it can handle more complex workloads.
Scaling up adds additional database servers to an existing running cluster to handle larger workloads.
e: In Snowflake, 'scaling up' refers to resizing a virtual warehouse to handle more complex workloads by increasing its computational resources, while 'scaling out' involves adding more clusters of the same size to a virtual warehouse to handle more concurrent queries.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition that has column-level security enabled?
e: Column-level security is available starting from the Enterprise edition of Snowflake. This feature allows granular access control at the column level within tables, ensuring enhanced security and compliance.

q: What parameter controls if the Virtual Warehouse starts immediately after the CREATE WAREHOUSE statement?
e: The 'INITIALLY_SUSPENDED = TRUE/FALSE' parameter controls whether the Virtual Warehouse starts immediately after the CREATE WAREHOUSE statement. If set to TRUE, the warehouse will not start automatically; if set to FALSE, it will start immediately upon creation.

q: When cloning a database, what is cloned with the database? (Choose two.)
o: Existing child objects within the database
Future child objects within the database
Privileges on the schemas within the database
Only schemas and tables within the database
e: When cloning a database in Snowflake, the operation clones the existing child objects within the database and the privileges on the schemas within the database. It does not clone privileges on the database itself or future child objects.

q: Which of the following describes the Snowflake Cloud Services layer?
o: Coordinates activities in the Snowflake account
Executes queries submitted by the Snowflake account users
Manages quotas on the Snowflake account storage
Manages the virtual warehouse cache to speed up queries
e: The Snowflake Cloud Services layer is responsible for coordinating activities within the Snowflake account. It serves as the central management hub for all tasks, including user authentication, query parsing and optimization, and metadata management.

q: What is the maximum total Continuous Data Protection (CDP) charges incurred for a temporary table?
e: The maximum total Continuous Data Protection (CDP) charges incurred for a temporary table in Snowflake is 24 hours. Temporary tables have a shorter CDP period compared to other table types.

q: When reviewing a query profile, what is a symptom that a query is too large to fit into the memory?
o: A single join node uses more than 50% of the query time
Partitions scanned is equal to partitions total
The query is spilling to remote storage
e: When reviewing a query profile in Snowflake, a symptom that a query is too large to fit into memory is when the query is spilling to remote storage. This indicates that the query's memory requirements exceed the available memory, causing Snowflake to use disk storage as an overflow.

q: What type of query benefits the MOST from search optimization?
o: A query that uses only disjunction (i.e., OR) predicates
A query that includes analytical expressions
A query that uses equality predicates or predicates that use IN
A query that filters on semi-structured data types
e: Search optimization in Snowflake is most beneficial for queries that use equality predicates or predicates that use IN. These types of queries can efficiently leverage search optimization to quickly find relevant data, leading to faster query execution.

q: What transformations are supported in a CREATE PIPE ... AS COPY ... FROM (..) statement? (Choose two.)
o: Data can be filtered by an optional WHERE clause.
Incoming data can be joined with other tables.
Row level access can be defined.
e: Using a query as the source for the COPY statement for column reordering, column omission, and casts (i.e. transforming data during a load) is supported. Note that only simple SELECT statements are supported. Filtering using a WHERE clause is not supported.

q: Which of the following are characteristics of Snowflake virtual warehouses? (Choose two.)
o: Auto-resume applies only to the last warehouse that was started in a multi-cluster warehouse.
The ability to auto-suspend a warehouse is only available in the Enterprise edition or above.
SnowSQL supports both a configuration file and a command line option for specifying a default warehouse.
A user cannot specify a default warehouse when using the ODBC driver.
The default virtual warehouse size can be changed at any time.
e:
- SnowSQL supports both a configuration file and a command line option for specifying a default warehouse.: SnowSQL permite especificar un warehouse predeterminado tanto a traves de un archivo de configuracion (~/.snowsql/config) como mediante opciones de linea de comandos (--warehouse).
- The default virtual warehouse size can be changed at any time.: El tamano de un virtual warehouse puede modificarse en cualquier momento mediante ALTER WAREHOUSE, sin necesidad de recrearlo.
- Auto-resume applies only to the last warehouse that was started in a multi-cluster warehouse.: Incorrecto. Auto-resume aplica a todos los clusters del warehouse, no solo al ultimo.
- The ability to auto-suspend a warehouse is only available in the Enterprise edition or above.: Incorrecto. Auto-suspend esta disponible en todas las ediciones de Snowflake.
- A user cannot specify a default warehouse when using the ODBC driver.: Incorrecto. El driver ODBC permite especificar un warehouse predeterminado en la configuracion de conexion.

q: Which command should be used to load data from a file, located in an external stage, into a table in Snowflake?
e: To load data from a file located in an external stage into a Snowflake table, the COPY command is used. This command allows for efficient data loading from files stored in stages like Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.

q: The Snowflake Cloud Data Platform is described as having which of the following architectures?
e: The architecture of the Snowflake Cloud Data Platform is best described as 'multi-cluster shared data'. This architecture allows for the separation of storage and compute resources, enabling efficient data management and scalable performance.

q: Which of the following is a data tokenization integration partner?
e: Protegrity is known for its data security solutions, including tokenization, and is a data tokenization integration partner with Snowflake. This partnership allows for enhanced data security within the Snowflake environment.

q: What versions of Snowflake should be used to manage compliance with Personal Identifiable Information (PII) requirements? (Choose two.)
e: The Business Critical Edition and Enterprise Edition of Snowflake are best suited for managing compliance with Personal Identifiable Information (PII) requirements, offering advanced security features necessary for handling sensitive data.

q: What are supported file formats for unloading data from Snowflake? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake supports various file formats for unloading data, including JSON, Parquet, and CSV.

q: The Snowflake cloud services layer is responsible for which tasks? (Choose two.)
e: The Snowflake cloud services layer is responsible for key management activities such as authentication and access control, ensuring secure access to data, and metadata management, which involves maintaining data about the data stored in Snowflake.

q: What is a key feature of Snowflake architecture?
o: Zero-copy cloning creates a mirror copy of a database that updates with the original.
Software updates are automatically applied on a quarterly basis.
Snowflake eliminates resource contention with its virtual warehouse implementation.
Multi-cluster warehouses allow users to run a query that spans across multiple clusters.
Snowflake automatically sorts DATE columns during ingest, for fast retrieval by date.
e: A key feature of Snowflake architecture is its virtual warehouse implementation, which eliminates resource contention. This allows for independent scaling of compute and storage, ensuring that workloads do not compete for resources.

q: When publishing a Snowflake Data Marketplace listing into a remote region what should be taken into consideration? (Choose two.)
o: There is no need to have a Snowflake account in the target region, a share will be created for each user.
The listing is replicated into all selected regions automatically, the data is not.
The user must have the ORGADMIN role available in at least one account to link accounts for replication.
Shares attached to listings in remote regions can be viewed from any account in an organization.
For a standard listing the user can wait until the first customer requests the data before replicating it to the target region.
e: When publishing a Snowflake Data Marketplace listing in a remote region, it's important to know that the listing is replicated across all selected regions, but the data itself is not automatically replicated. Additionally, you do not need to replicate the data to each region until a consumer requests it.

q: When loading data into Snowflake via Snowpipe what is the compressed file size recommendation?
e: When using Snowpipe to load data into Snowflake, the recommended size for compressed files is between 100 and 250 MB. This size range offers an optimal balance between upload efficiency and processing speed.

q: Which Snowflake feature allows a user to substitute a randomly generated identifier for sensitive data, in order to prevent unauthorized users access to the data, before loading it into Snowflake?
e: External Tokenization is a feature in Snowflake that allows users to replace sensitive data with a randomly generated identifier before loading it into Snowflake. This process ensures that sensitive information remains secure by preventing unauthorized access.

q: Which of the following are examples of operations that require a Virtual Warehouse to complete, assuming no queries have been executed previously? (Choose three.)
e: MIN(<<column value>>) can be answered directly from micro-partition metadata (metadata cache), so it does not require a running virtual warehouse. COPY loads data, SUM(<<column value>>) must scan column values, and UPDATE is a DML operation - these three require a virtual warehouse.

q: What is the SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE view that contains information about which objects were read by queries within the last 365 days (1 year)?
e: The 'ACCESS_HISTORY' view within the SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE schema provides information about the objects that were accessed by queries in the last 365 days. This view is instrumental in auditing and understanding data access patterns within Snowflake.

q: Which feature is only available in the Enterprise or higher editions of Snowflake?
e: Column-level security is a feature exclusive to the Enterprise or higher editions of Snowflake. It allows for granular control over access to specific columns within a table, enhancing data security and privacy.

q: Will data cached in a warehouse be lost when the warehouse is resized?
o: Possibly, if the warehouse is resized to a smaller size and the cache no longer fits.
Yes, because the compute resource is replaced in its entirety with a new compute resource.
No, because the size of the cache is independent from the warehouse size.
Yes, because the new compute resource will no longer have access to the cache encryption key.
e: Decreasing the size of a running warehouse removes compute resources from the warehouse. When the computer resources are removed, the cache associated with those resources is dropped, which can impact performance in the same way that suspending the warehouse can impact performance after it is resumed.

q: Which semi-structured file formats are supported when unloading data from a table? (Choose two.)
e: When unloading data from a table in Snowflake, the supported semi-structured file formats include JSON and Parquet. These formats are widely used for handling semi-structured data due to their flexibility and compatibility with various data processing tools.

q: A running virtual warehouse is suspended. What is the MINIMUM amount of time that the warehouse will incur charges for when it is restarted?
e: When a running virtual warehouse in Snowflake is suspended and then restarted, the minimum amount of time for which it will incur charges is 60 seconds. This is the minimum billing unit for compute resources in Snowflake.

q: What are the responsibilities of Snowflake's Cloud Service layer? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake's Cloud Service layer is responsible for authentication, ensuring secure access to data; query parsing and optimization, which involves analyzing and optimizing queries for execution; and resource management, which includes managing the allocation and scaling of resources.

q: How long is the Fail-safe period for temporary and transient tables?
o: There is no Fail-safe period for these tables.
e: Temporary and transient tables in Snowflake do not have a Fail-safe period. Fail-safe is a feature that provides additional protection for data stored in permanent tables, but it does not apply to temporary or transient tables.

q: Which command should be used to download files from a Snowflake stage to a local folder on a client's machine?
e: To download files from a Snowflake stage to a local folder, the GET command is used. This command allows users to retrieve data from a Snowflake stage and save it to a specified local directory.

q: How does Snowflake Fail-safe protect data in a permanent table?
o: Fail-safe makes data available up to 1 day, recoverable by user operations.
Fail-safe makes data available for 7 days, recoverable by user operations.
Fail-safe makes data available for 7 days, recoverable only by Snowflake Support.
Fail-safe makes data available up to 1 day, recoverable only by Snowflake Support.
e: Snowflake's Fail-safe feature for permanent tables ensures that data is available for a period of 7 days after it is no longer accessible through the standard Snowflake interface. During this period, the data can only be recovered by Snowflake Support, providing an extra layer of protection against data loss.

q: A virtual warehouse is created using the following command: Create warehouse my_WH with - warehouse_size = MEDIUM min_cluster_count = 1 max_cluster_count = 1 auto_suspend = 60 auto_resume = true; The image below is a graphical representation of the warehouse utilization across two days. What action should be taken to address this situation?
o: Increase the warehouse size from Medium to 2XL.
Increase the value for the parameter MAX_CONCURRENCY_LEVEL.
Configure the warehouse to a multi-cluster warehouse.
Lower the value of the parameter STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS.
e:
- Configure the warehouse to a multi-cluster warehouse: Permitir múltiples clústeres ayuda a manejar la carga alta de trabajo al agregar recursos dinámicamente, eliminando las colas de consultas.
- Increase the warehouse size from Medium to 2XL: Aumentar el tamaño mejora la capacidad de un clúster, pero no resuelve problemas de concurrencia en cargas simultáneas altas.
- Increase the value for the parameter MAX_CONCURRENCY_LEVEL: Esto aumenta las consultas concurrentes permitidas, pero sigue limitado por los recursos de un único clúster.
- Lower the value of the parameter STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS: Reducir este valor haría que las consultas fallaran más rápido en lugar de resolver la congestión.

q: Which minimum Snowflake edition allows for a dedicated metadata store?
e: The Virtual Private Snowflake edition of Snowflake is the minimum level that allows for a dedicated metadata store. This feature provides enhanced security and performance, especially for organizations with large or sensitive datasets.

q: Network policies can be set at which Snowflake levels? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, network policies can be set at the User and Account levels. These policies define the IP address ranges that are allowed or denied access to your Snowflake account, enhancing security by restricting unauthorized network access.

q: What are the correct parameters for time travel and fail-safe in the Snowflake Enterprise Edition?
o: Default Time Travel Retention is set to 0 days. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 30 days. Fail Safe retention time is 1 day.
Default Time Travel Retention is set to 1 day. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 365 days. Fail Safe retention time is 7 days.
Default Time Travel Retention is set to 0 days. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 90 days. Fail Safe retention time is 7 days.
Default Time Travel Retention is set to 1 day. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 90 days. Fail Safe retention time is 7 days.
Default Time Travel Retention is set to 7 days. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 1 day. Fail Safe retention time is 90 days.
Default Time Travel Retention is set to 90 days. Maximum Time Travel Retention is 7 days. Fail Safe retention time is 356 days.
e: For the Snowflake Enterprise Edition, the default Time Travel retention is 1 day, with a maximum of 90 days. The Fail Safe period, which provides additional protection for your data, is set to 7 days.

q: Which of the following objects are contained within a schema? (Choose two.)
e: Within a Snowflake schema, objects such as Streams and External tables are contained. Streams enable change data capture on tables, while External tables allow querying data stored in external storage without loading it into Snowflake.

q: Which of the following statements describe features of Snowflake data caching? (Choose two.)
o: When a virtual warehouse is suspended, the data cache is saved on the remote storage layer.
When the data cache is full, the least-recently used data will be cleared to make room.
A user can only access their own queries from the query result cache.
A user must set USE_METADATA_CACHE to TRUE to use the metadata cache in queries.
The RESULT_SCAN table function can access and filter the contents of the query result cache.
e: In Snowflake, when the data cache is full, it automatically clears the least recently used data to make room for new data. Additionally, the RESULT_SCAN table function allows users to access and filter the contents of the query result cache, providing efficient access to recent query results.

q: A table needs to be loaded. The input data is in JSON format and is a concatenation of multiple JSON documents. The file size is 3 GB. A warehouse size S is being used. The following COPY INTO command was executed: COPY INTO SAMPLE FROM @~/SAMPLE.JSON (TYPE=JSON) The load failed with this error: Max LOB size (16777216) exceeded, actual size of parsed column is 17894470. How can this issue be resolved?
o: Compress the file and load the compressed file.
Split the file into multiple files in the recommended size range (100 MB - 250 MB).
Set STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY=TRUE in the COPY INTO command.
e: If the data exceeds 16 MB, enable the STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY file format option for the COPY INTO <table> command to remove the outer array structure and load the records into separate table row.

q: What is a feature of a stored procedure in Snowflake?
o: They can be created as secure and hide the underlying metadata from all users.
They can access tables from a single database.
They can only contain a single SQL statement.
They can be created to run with a caller's rights or an owner's rights.
e: Stored procedures in Snowflake can be created to execute with either the caller's rights or the owner's rights. This feature allows for flexibility in managing security and access control when executing stored procedures.

q: Which columns are part of the result set of the Snowflake LATERAL FLATTEN command? (Choose two.)
e: The LATERAL FLATTEN command in Snowflake produces a result set with these output columns: SEQ, KEY, PATH, INDEX, VALUE, and THIS. PATH indicates the path to each element within a semi-structured data type, and INDEX provides the positional index of each element within an array. CONTENT, BYTE_SIZE, and DATATYPE are not columns produced by FLATTEN.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition required to create a materialized view?
e: The creation of materialized views in Snowflake requires at least the Enterprise Edition. This edition provides the necessary features and capabilities to support materialized views, which are used for performance optimization.

q: Which Snowflake function will interpret an input string as a JSON document, and produce a VARIANT value?
e: The parse_json() function in Snowflake is used to interpret an input string as a JSON document and produce a VARIANT value. This function is essential for handling and querying JSON data within Snowflake.

q: How are serverless features billed?
o: Per second multiplied by an automatic sizing for the job
Per minute multiplied by an automatic sizing for the job, with a minimum of one minute
Per second multiplied by the size, as determined by the SERVERLESS_FEATURES_SIZE account parameter
Serverless features are not billed, unless the total cost for the month exceeds 10% of the warehouse credits, on the account
e: Serverless features in Snowflake are billed per second, multiplied by an automatic sizing for the job. This billing method ensures that users are charged based on the actual usage and computational resources required for serverless operations.

q: Which Snowflake architectural layer is responsible for a query execution plan?
e: The Cloud services layer in Snowflake's architecture is responsible for generating a query execution plan. This layer handles tasks like query parsing, optimization, and metadata management, essential for formulating an efficient execution strategy.

q: When unloading to a stage, which of the following is a recommended practice or approach?
o: Set SINGLE = TRUE for larger files.
Avoid the use of the CAST function.
e: When unloading data to a stage in Snowflake, it is recommended to define an individual file format. This ensures that the data is unloaded in a format that is optimized for the intended use, enhancing compatibility and efficiency in data handling.

q: Which SQL commands, when committed, will consume a stream and advance the stream offset? (Choose two.)
o: INSERT INTO TABLE SELECT FROM STREAM
ALTER TABLE AS SELECT FROM STREAM
e: A stream advances the offset only when it is used in a DML transaction.

q: Which methods can be used to delete staged files from a Snowflake stage? (Choose two.)
o: Use the DROP command after the load completes.
Specify the TEMPORARY option when creating the file format.
Specify the PURGE copy option in the COPY INTO command.
Use the REMOVE command after the load completes.
Use the DELETE LOAD HISTORY command after the load completes.
e: To delete staged files in Snowflake, you can specify the PURGE copy option in the COPY INTO command, which deletes files immediately after successful loading, or use the REMOVE command after the load completes to manually delete the files.

q: On which of the following cloud platforms can a Snowflake account be hosted? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake can be hosted on Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure Cloud, and Google Cloud Platform. These platforms provide the necessary infrastructure and services to support Snowflake's cloud data platform, offering scalability, reliability, and a range of cloud-based capabilities.

q: What Snowflake role must be granted for a user to create and manage accounts?
