q: For non-materialized views, what column in Information Schema and Account Usage identifies whether a view is secure or not?
e: For non-materialized views in Snowflake, the 'IS_SECURE' column in the Information Schema and Account Usage identifies whether a view is secure or not. This column provides information on the security status of the view.

q: The bulk data load history that is available upon completion of the COPY statement is stored where and for how long?
o: In the metadata of the target table for 14 days
In the metadata of the pipe for 14 days
In the metadata of the target table for 64 days
In the metadata of the pipe for 64 days
e: Bulk data load history (via COPY statement) is stored in the metadata of the target table for 64 days. This is distinct from Snowpipe load history, which is stored in the metadata of the pipe for 14 days. The 14-day retention applies only to Snowpipe continuous loading, not to bulk COPY operations.

q: User INQUISITIVE_PERSON has been granted the role DATA_SCIENCE. The role DATA_SCIENCE has privileges OWNERSHIP on the schema MARKETING of the database ANALYTICS_DW. Which command will show all privileges granted to that schema?
e: To view all privileges granted to the schema 'MARKETING' of the database 'ANALYTICS_DW', the command 'SHOW GRANTS ON SCHEMA ANALYTICS_DW.MARKETING' should be used. This command displays the permissions associated with the specified schema.

q: Which of the following are characteristics of security in Snowflake?
o: Account and user authentication is only available with the Snowflake Business Critical edition.
Support for HIPAA and GDPR compliance is available for UI Snowflake editions.
Periodic rekeying of encrypted data is available with the Snowflake Enterprise edition and higher
Private communication to internal stages is allowed in the Snowflake Enterprise edition and higher.
e: A key characteristic of security in Snowflake is the periodic rekeying of encrypted data, which is available with the Snowflake Enterprise edition and higher. This feature enhances data security by periodically changing the encryption keys used to protect stored data.

q: Which of the following objects can be shared through secure data sharing?
e: In Snowflake's secure data sharing, external tables can be shared with consumers. Secure data sharing allows sharing of database objects like tables and views, including external tables, without copying or moving data.

q: Which formats does Snowflake store semi-structured data in? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake stores semi-structured data internally using the ARRAY and OBJECT types (inside VARIANT). XML and GeoJSON are supported input formats, not internal storage formats, and BLOB is not a Snowflake data type.

q: A user is preparing to load data from an external stage. Which practice will provide the MOST efficient loading performance?
o: Store the files on the external stage to ensure caching is maintained
Use pattern matching for regular expression execution
Load the data in one large file
e: Organizing files into logical paths is an efficient practice for loading data from an external stage in Snowflake. This helps in managing and categorizing the files effectively, making the data load process more streamlined and efficient.

q: What effect does WAIT_FOR_COMPLETION = TRUE have when running an ALTER WAREHOUSE command and changing the warehouse size?
o: The warehouse size does not change until all queries currently running in the warehouse have completed.
The warehouse size does not change until all queries currently in the warehouse queue have completed.
The warehouse size does not change until the warehouse is suspended and restarted.
It does not return from the command until the warehouse has finished changing its size.
e: Setting WAIT_FOR_COMPLETION = TRUE in the ALTER WAREHOUSE command in Snowflake means that the command will not return until the warehouse has finished changing its size. This ensures that the resize operation is completed before the command returns control.

q: Which of the following can be used when unloading data from Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: When unloading semi-structured data, it is recommended that the STRIP_OUTER_ARRAY option be used.
Use the ENCODING file format option to change the encoding from the default UTF-8.
The OBJECT_CONSTRUCT function can be used to convert relational data to semi-structured data.
By using the SINGLE = TRUE parameter, a single file up to 5 GB in size can be exported to the storage layer.
Use the PARSE_JSON function to ensure structured data will be unloaded into the VARIANT data type.
e: When unloading data from Snowflake, the ENCODING file format option allows users to change the character encoding from the default UTF-8. The SINGLE = TRUE parameter facilitates exporting data as a single file up to 5 GB in size, which can be useful for large data sets.

q: What data is stored in the Snowflake storage layer? (Choose two.)
e: The storage layer holds table data as micro-partitions and also the persisted query results (result cache). Parameters, query history and view definitions live in the cloud services layer, not in the storage layer.

q: A data provider wants to share data with a consumer who does not have a Snowflake account. The provider creates a reader account for the consumer following these steps: Based on this configuration what is true of the reader account?
o: Created a database to hold the share and an extra-small warehouse to query the data
Granted the role PUBLIC the following privileges: Usage on the warehouse, database, and schema, and SELECT on all the objects in the share
The reader account will automatically use the Standard edition of Snowflake.
The reader account compute will be billed to the provider account.
The reader account can clone data the provider has shared, but cannot re-share it.
The reader account can create a copy of the shared data using CREATE TABLE AS...
e: In Snowflake, when a data provider creates a reader account for a consumer, the compute resources used by the reader account are billed to the provider's account. Additionally, the reader account can clone the shared data but is not allowed to re-share it.

q: Which of the following activities consume virtual warehouse credits in the Snowflake environment? (Choose two.)
e: In the Snowflake environment, running a custom query and running COPY commands consume virtual warehouse credits. These activities require computational resources, and thus, the credits are used as a measure of the compute time consumed.

q: When loading data into Snowflake, the COPY command supports which of the following?
e: When using the COPY command to load data into Snowflake, it supports column reordering. This feature allows the data being loaded to be reordered to match the column order of the target table, facilitating flexible data loading.

q: What is cached during a query on a virtual warehouse?
o: Any columns accessed during the query
The columns in the result set of the query
All rows accessed during the query
e: During a query on a virtual warehouse in Snowflake, any columns accessed during the query are cached. This caching mechanism helps improve performance by reducing the need to access the same data repeatedly from the storage layer.

q: What is the default character set used when loading CSV files into Snowflake?
e: When loading CSV files into Snowflake, the default character set used is UTF-8. This character encoding supports a wide range of characters and is commonly used for text data.

q: Which of the following describes external functions in Snowflake?
o: They are a type of User-defined Function (UDF).
They contain their own SQL code.
They call code that is stored inside of Snowflake.
They can return multiple rows for each row received.
e: External functions in Snowflake are a type of User-Defined Function (UDF). Unlike regular UDFs, external functions do not contain their own code within Snowflake. Instead, they call code executed outside of Snowflake through a proxy service (such as AWS API Gateway or Azure API Management) that relays requests to a remote service (like AWS Lambda or Azure Functions). They are scalar functions that return one row for each row received.

q: Which of the following are valid methods for authenticating users for access into Snowflake? (Choose three.)
e: For authenticating users into Snowflake, federated authentication, key-pair authentication, and OAuth are valid methods. Federated authentication allows integration with identity providers, key-pair authentication uses cryptographic keys, and OAuth is a standard for access delegation.

q: A user has a standard multi-cluster warehouse auto-scaling policy in place. Which condition will trigger a cluster to shut-down?
o: When after 2-3 consecutive checks the system determines that the load on the most-loaded cluster could be redistributed.
When after 5-6 consecutive checks the system determines that the load on the most-loaded cluster could be redistributed.
When after 5-6 consecutive checks the system determines that the load on the least-loaded cluster could be redistributed.
When after 2-3 consecutive checks the system determines that the load on the least-loaded cluster could be redistributed.
e: In Snowflake's standard multi-cluster warehouse auto-scaling policy, a cluster will shut down when, after 5-6 consecutive checks, the system determines that the load on the least-loaded cluster could be redistributed to other clusters. This helps in optimizing resource usage and cost.

q: What is the minimum Snowflake edition needed for database failover and fail-back between Snowflake accounts for business continuity and disaster recovery?
e: The minimum Snowflake edition required for database failover and fail-back between Snowflake accounts, which are crucial for business continuity and disaster recovery, is the Business Critical edition. This edition provides advanced features for high availability and security.

q: How would a user execute a series of SQL statements using a task?
o: Include the SQL statements in the body of the task CREATE TASK mytask .. AS INSERT INTO target1 SELECT .. FROM stream_s1 WHERE .. INSERT INTO target2 SELECT .. FROM stream_s1 WHERE ..

A stored procedure can have only one DML statement per stored procedure invocation and therefore the user should sequence stored procedure calls in the task definition CREATE TASK mytask 	AS call stored_proc1(); call stored_proc2();
Use a stored procedure executing multiple SQL statements and invoke the stored procedure from the task. CREATE TASK mytask
Create a task for each SQL statement (e.g. resulting in task1, task2, etc.) and string the series of SQL statements by having a control task calling task1, task2, etc. sequentially.
e: To execute a series of SQL statements using a task in Snowflake, a user should use a stored procedure that executes multiple SQL statements and then invoke this stored procedure from the task. This method allows multiple statements to be executed in sequence within a single task.

q: How many resource monitors can be assigned at the account level?
e: At the account level in Snowflake, only one resource monitor can be assigned. This resource monitor is used to track and manage the overall resource usage and credits consumption for the entire Snowflake account.

q: Data storage for individual tables can be monitored using which commands and/or objects? (Choose two.)
e: To monitor data storage for individual tables in Snowflake, the 'SHOW STORAGE BY TABLE;' command and the 'TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS' object in the Information Schema can be used. These tools provide detailed insights into the storage utilization of each table.

q: How would a user run a multi-cluster warehouse in maximized mode?
o: Configure the maximum clusters setting to 'Maximum.'
Turn on the additional clusters manually after starting the warehouse.
Set the minimum Clusters and maximum Clusters settings to the same value.
Set the minimum clusters and maximum clusters settings to different values.
e: To run a multi-cluster warehouse in maximized mode in Snowflake, the user should set both the minimum and maximum clusters settings to the same value. This configuration ensures that the maximum number of clusters are always running, providing maximized compute resources.

q: What internal stages are available in Snowflake? (Choose three.)
e: In Snowflake, the internal stages available are Named stage, User stage, and Table stage. These stages are used for different purposes: Named stage for storing files temporarily, User stage for individual user file storage, and Table stage for storing files associated with a specific table.

q: Which stages are used with the Snowflake PUT command to upload files from a local file system? (Choose three.)
e: The PUT command in Snowflake is used to upload files from a local file system to Snowflake. This command can be used with a User Stage, Table Stage, or an Internal Named Stage. These stages are designed to temporarily store files before they are loaded into Snowflake tables.

q: Which data type can store more than one type of data structure?
e: The VARIANT data type in Snowflake is capable of storing multiple types of data structures. It is used for semi-structured data and can store JSON, XML, AVRO, or other formats in a single column.

q: User-level network policies can be created by which of the following roles? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, user-level network policies can be created and managed by the ACCOUNTADMIN and SECURITYADMIN roles. These roles have the necessary privileges to manage security and access settings, including network policies.

q: What SQL command would be used to view all roles that were granted to USER1?
e: The command 'show grants to user USER1;' is used in Snowflake to display all roles that have been granted to a specific user, in this case, USER1. This command provides information about user permissions and role assignments.

q: Which ACCOUNT_USAGE views are used to evaluate the details of dynamic data masking? (Choose two.)
e: The ACCOUNT_USAGE views 'POLICY_REFERENCES' and 'MASKING_POLICIES' in Snowflake are used to evaluate the details of dynamic data masking. These views provide information about the masking policies applied and their references across the database.

q: Which of the following are considerations when using a directory table when working with unstructured data? (Choose two.)
o: A directory table is a separate database object.
Directory tables store data file metadata.
A directory table will be automatically added to a stage.
Directory tables do not have their own grantable privileges.
Directory table data cannot be refreshed manually.
e: Directory tables are implicit objects layered on stages, store file-level metadata about staged files, and have no grantable privileges of their own. Therefore, the two correct considerations are that they store data file metadata and that they do not have their own grantable privileges.

q: The first user assigned to a new account, ACCOUNTADMIN, should create at least one additional user with which administrative privilege?
e: For a new Snowflake account, the first user assigned as ACCOUNTADMIN should create at least one additional user with the USERADMIN privilege. This administrative privilege is essential for managing users and roles within the Snowflake environment.

q: Which statement describes how Snowflake supports reader accounts?
o: A reader account can consume data from the provider account that created it and combine it with its own data.
A consumer needs to become a licensed Snowflake customer as data sharing is only supported between Snowflake accounts.
The users in a reader account can query data that has been shared with the reader account and can perform DML tasks.
The SHOW MANAGED ACCOUNTS command will view all the reader accounts that have been created for an account.
e: The SHOW MANAGED ACCOUNTS command is used to view all reader accounts created for a provider account. (A) is incorrect because reader accounts can only consume data from the provider -- they cannot upload new data, modify existing data, or perform DML operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE), so they cannot 'combine with its own data.' (B) is incorrect because reader accounts exist precisely so consumers do NOT need a Snowflake license. (C) is incorrect because reader accounts cannot perform DML tasks -- they are restricted to querying shared data.

q: How does Snowflake allow a data provider with an Azure account in central Canada to share data with a data consumer on AWS in Australia?
o: The data provider in Azure Central Canada can create a direct share to AWS Asia Pacific, if they are both in the same organization.
The data consumer and data provider can form a Data Exchange within the same organization to create a share from Azure Central Canada to AWS Asia Pacific.
The data provider uses the GET DATA workflow in the Snowflake Data Marketplace to create a share between Azure Central Canada and AWS Asia Pacific.
The data provider must replicate the database to a secondary account in AWS Asia Pacific within the same organization then create a share to the data consumer's account
e: In Snowflake, a data provider with an Azure account in Central Canada can share data with a data consumer on AWS in Australia by replicating the database to a secondary account in AWS Asia Pacific within the same organization. After replication, they can create a share to the data consumer's account, enabling cross-cloud data sharing.

q: Which Snowflake objects can be shared with other Snowflake accounts? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake secure data sharing supports sharing tables, secure views (and secure materialized views) and secure UDFs with other Snowflake accounts. Roles and stored procedures cannot be shared; databases and schemas are containers on which usage is granted, not shared objects themselves.

q: Which Snowflake feature will allow small volumes of data to continuously load into Snowflake and will incrementally make the data available for analysis?
e: The CREATE PIPE command in Snowflake is used to create a Snowpipe, which allows for the continuous and incremental loading of data into Snowflake. Snowpipe automatically loads data as soon as it becomes available in a cloud storage location, making it suitable for small and continuous data loads.

q: Which Snowflake partner specializes in data catalog solutions?
e: Alation is a Snowflake partner that specializes in data catalog solutions. Alation provides a collaborative data catalog platform that helps organizations find, understand, and govern their data.

q: Which of the following can be executed/called with Snowpipe?
e: Snowpipe in Snowflake is designed to work with a single COPY INTO statement. This command is used to load data from a file stage (like an S3 bucket) into a Snowflake table. Snowpipe automates this process by continuously checking for new files in the stage and loading them as they arrive.

q: Which Snowflake objects will incur both storage and cloud compute charges? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, both materialized views and transient tables incur storage and compute charges. Materialized views store query results physically, thereby incurring storage costs. Transient tables, like other tables, incur storage costs for the data they hold and compute costs when they are accessed or manipulated.

q: What file formats does Snowflake support for loading semi-structured data? (Choose three.)
e: Snowflake supports several file formats for loading semi-structured data, including JSON, Avro, and Parquet. These formats allow for efficient storage and querying of semi-structured data within Snowflake.

q: Which of the following statements about data sharing are true? (Choose two.)
o: New objects created by a Data Provider are automatically shared with existing Data Consumers and Reader Accounts.
All database objects can be included in a shared database.
Reader Accounts are created by Data Providers.
Reader Accounts are charged for warehouse usage.
e: In Snowflake data sharing, Reader Accounts are created by Data Providers to share data with consumers who don't have a Snowflake account. Shared databases are read-only to ensure data integrity and security, preventing Data Consumers from modifying the shared data.

q: Credit charges for Snowflake virtual warehouses are calculated based on which of the following considerations? (Choose two.)
o: The number of active users assigned to the warehouse
The size of the virtual warehouse
The length of time the warehouse is running
The duration of the queries that are executed
e: Credit charges for Snowflake virtual warehouses are determined by the size of the virtual warehouse and the length of time the warehouse is running. Larger warehouses and longer run times will consume more credits.

q: Which of the following are handled by the cloud services layer of the Snowflake architecture? (Choose two.)
e: The cloud services layer of the Snowflake architecture handles security and authentication and access control. This layer ensures secure data storage, processing, and access, managing user authentication and enforcing security policies.

q: What is a responsibility of Snowflake’s virtual warehouses?
e: In Snowflake, the primary responsibility of virtual warehouses is query execution. These warehouses are compute clusters that execute data processing tasks and queries, separate from storage and other management functions.

q: What features does Snowflake Time Travel enable?
o: Querying data-related objects that were created within the past 365 days
Restoring data-related objects that have been deleted within the past 90 days
Conducting point-in-time analysis for BI reporting
Analyzing data usage/manipulation over all periods of time
e: Snowflake Time Travel enables users to restore data-related objects that have been deleted within the past 90 days and conduct point-in-time analysis for BI reporting. This feature allows accessing historical data states for analysis and recovery purposes.

q: Which of the following statements describes a schema in Snowflake?
o: A logical grouping of objects that belongs to a single database
A logical grouping of objects that belongs to multiple databases
A named Snowflake object that includes all the information required to share a database
A uniquely identified Snowflake account within a business entity
e: In Snowflake, a schema is a logical grouping of database objects such as tables, views, and functions, and it belongs to a single database. Schemas help organize and manage these objects within the database.

q: What is the recommended compressed file size range for continuous data loads using Snowpipe?
e: The recommended compressed file size for data loads (including Snowpipe) is 100-250 MB or larger. This applies to both bulk data loads and Snowpipe continuous loading. Files of this size optimize parallel processing and reduce per-file overhead costs. Smaller files increase overhead, while very large files risk long load times.

q: How long is Snowpipe data load history retained?
o: As configured in the CREATE PIPE settings
e: Snowpipe load history metadata is retained for 14 days. The Snowflake documentation states that pipes only maintain the load history metadata for 14 days, so the correct option is 14 days.

q: A company strongly encourages all Snowflake users to self-enroll in Snowflake's default Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) service to provide increased login security for users connecting to Snowflake. Which application will the Snowflake users need to install on their devices in order to connect with MFA?
e: Snowflake's default Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) service uses Duo Security. Therefore, Snowflake users looking to connect with MFA should install the Duo Mobile application on their devices to complete the MFA process.

q: Which URL type allows users to access unstructured data without authenticating into Snowflake or passing an authorization token?
e: A pre-signed URL allows users to access unstructured data stored in cloud storage without the need for authenticating into Snowflake or passing an authorization token. This URL includes a signature that grants temporary access to the data.

q: Where would a Snowflake user find information about query activity from 90 days ago?
e: Snowflake users would find query activity from 90 days ago in the ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY view, because it retains query history for the last 365 days (1 year).

q: A marketing co-worker has requested the ability to change a warehouse size on their medium virtual warehouse called MKTG_WH. Which of the following statements will accommodate this request?
o: ALLOW RESIZE ON WAREHOUSE MKTG_WH TO USER MKTG_LEAD;
GRANT MODIFY ON WAREHOUSE MKTG_WH TO ROLE MARKETING;
GRANT MODIFY ON WAREHOUSE MKTG_WH TO USER MKTG_LEAD;
GRANT OPERATE ON WAREHOUSE MKTG_WH TO ROLE MARKET;
e: To accommodate the request to change the warehouse size for MKTG_WH, the statement 'GRANT MODIFY ON WAREHOUSE MKTG_WH TO ROLE MARKETING;' should be used. This grants the necessary privileges to the marketing role, allowing users with this role to modify the warehouse size.

q: Which of the following commands cannot be used within a reader account?
e: Within a reader account in Snowflake, the command 'CREATE SHARE' cannot be used. Reader accounts are typically limited in terms of data sharing capabilities, and they cannot create shares to distribute data to other accounts.

q: Which TABLE function helps to convert semi-structured data to a relational representation?
e: The 'FLATTEN' TABLE function in Snowflake is used to convert semi-structured data into a relational format. This function is particularly useful for unpacking nested data structures like JSON arrays and objects into a format that can be easily queried with SQL.

q: Which query profile statistics help determine if efficient pruning is occurring? (Choose two.)
e: To determine if efficient pruning is occurring in Snowflake, the 'Partitions total' and 'Partitions scanned' statistics in the query profile are helpful. These statistics indicate how many partitions exist and how many were actually scanned, reflecting the efficiency of pruning in reducing the amount of data processed.

q: What are the default Time Travel and Fail-safe retention periods for transient tables?
o: Transient tables are retained in neither Fail-safe nor Time Travel.
e: For transient tables in Snowflake, the default Time Travel retention period is 1 day. However, transient tables do not have a Fail-safe period. This means that they are only protected by Time Travel for the specified duration.

q: Which command is used to unload data from a Snowflake table into a file in a stage?
e: The 'COPY INTO' command in Snowflake is used to unload data from a table and export it to a file in a stage. This command enables data extraction and storage in a specified file format in an external stage or cloud storage location.

q: What are advantages clones have over tables created with CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement? (Choose two.)
o: The clone always stays in sync with the original table.
The clone has better query performance.
The clone is created almost instantly.
The clone will have time travel history from the original table.
The clone saves space by not duplicating storage.
e: Clones in Snowflake have the advantages of being created almost instantly and saving storage space, as they do not duplicate the data from the original table. Instead, clones use Snowflake's unique architecture to maintain separate metadata while sharing the same underlying data files.

q: How often are the Account and Table master keys automatically rotated by Snowflake?
e: Snowflake automatically rotates keys in its managed key hierarchy, including account and table master keys, every 30 days (when they are more than 30 days old).

q: Which privilege is required for a role to be able to resume a suspended warehouse if auto-resume is not enabled?
e: The 'OPERATE' privilege is required for a role to resume a suspended warehouse in Snowflake when auto-resume is not enabled. This privilege allows the role to start and stop the warehouse as needed.

q: Which statement MOST accurately describes clustering in Snowflake?
o: The database ACCOUNTADMIN must define the clustering methodology for each Snowflake table.
Clustering is the way data is grouped together and stored within Snowflake micro-partitions.
The clustering key must be included in the COPY command when loading data into Snowflake.
Clustering can be disabled within a Snowflake account.
e: Clustering in Snowflake refers to how data is grouped and stored within micro-partitions. It optimizes data storage and access by organizing data based on certain key(s), known as clustering keys, but does not necessarily require involvement from the ACCOUNTADMIN or specific commands during data loading.

q: Which of the following practices are recommended when creating a user in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: Configure the user to be initially disabled.
Set a default role for the user.
Set the number of minutes to unlock to 15 minutes.
Set the user's access to expire within a specified timeframe.
e: When creating a user in Snowflake, it is recommended to force an immediate password change to ensure security and set a default role for ease of access and control. These practices enhance security and user experience in the Snowflake environment.

q: Network policies can be applied to which of the following Snowflake objects? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, network policies can be applied to 'Users' and 'Accounts'. These policies control the network addresses (IP addresses) from which users can connect to Snowflake, enhancing the security of the account and its users.

q: Where is Snowflake metadata stored?
e: Snowflake metadata is stored in the cloud services layer. This layer is a key component of Snowflake's architecture, responsible for managing all aspects of the data warehouse, including metadata management, query compilation, and optimization.

q: What columns are returned when performing a FLATTEN command on semi-structured data? (Choose two.)
e: When using the FLATTEN command on semi-structured data in Snowflake, the columns returned typically include 'KEY' and 'VALUE'. 'KEY' represents the path to the element in the semi-structured data, while 'VALUE' contains the data element from the path specified.

q: Which of the following Snowflake features provide continuous data protection automatically? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake's Time Travel and Fail-safe are the features that provide continuous data protection automatically. Time Travel allows users to access historical data within a defined retention period. Fail-safe provides an additional layer of data protection by maintaining historical data beyond the Time Travel period for recovery by Snowflake support.

q: A developer is granted ownership of a table that has a masking policy. The developer’s role is not able to see the masked data. Will the developer be able to modify the table to read the masked data?
o: Yes, because a table owner has full control and can unset masking policies.
Yes, because masking policies only apply to cloned tables.
No, because masking policies must always reference specific access roles.
No, because ownership of a table does not include the ability to change masking policies.
e: Even if a developer is granted ownership of a table with a masking policy, they will not be able to modify the table to read the masked data if their role does not have the required permissions. Ownership of the table does not automatically confer the ability to change or unset masking policies.

q: How should a virtual warehouse be configured if a user wants to ensure that additional multi-clusters are resumed with no delay?
o: Configure the warehouse to a size larger than generally required
Set the minimum and maximum clusters to autoscale
Use the standard warehouse scaling policy
Use the economy warehouse scaling policy
e: To ensure that additional multi-clusters in a virtual warehouse are resumed with no delay, the warehouse should be configured with autoscaling by setting the minimum and maximum number of clusters. This setup allows Snowflake to automatically manage the number of clusters based on the workload.

q: During periods of warehouse contention, which parameter controls the maximum length of time a warehouse will hold a query for processing?
e: The 'STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS' parameter controls the maximum length of time a warehouse will hold a query in a queued state before processing it. This parameter is important during periods of warehouse contention to manage query execution times.

q: Files have been uploaded to a Snowflake internal stage. The files now need to be deleted. Which SQL command should be used to delete the files?
e: To delete files from a Snowflake internal stage, the 'REMOVE' SQL command is used. This command allows users to specify the files to be deleted from the staged location.

q: In a Snowflake role hierarchy, what is the top-level role?
e: In the role hierarchy of Snowflake, the top-level role is 'ACCOUNTADMIN'. This role has the highest level of privileges, including the ability to manage all aspects of the Snowflake account, from user and role management to warehouse and database administration.

q: By default, which Snowflake role is required to create a share?
e: By default, the 'ACCOUNTADMIN' role is required to create a share in Snowflake. This role has the necessary permissions to manage and share data across different accounts or organizations within Snowflake.

q: What happens to historical data when the retention period for an object ends?
o: The data is cloned into a historical object.
Time Travel on the historical data is dropped.
The object containing the historical data is dropped.
e: When the Time Travel retention period ends, historical data moves into Fail-safe. Fail-safe provides a non-configurable 7-day period during which data may be recoverable only by Snowflake Support. The data is not dropped or cloned -- it transitions from the Time Travel state (user-accessible) to the Fail-safe state (only Snowflake can recover it). After Fail-safe expires, data is permanently purged.

q: A company’s security audit requires generating a report listing all Snowflake logins (e.g., date and user) within the last 90 days. Which of the following statements will return the required information? FROM table(information_schema.login_history_by_user())
e: To generate a report listing all Snowflake logins within the last 90 days, the statement 'SELECT EVENT_TIMESTAMP, USER_NAME FROM ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY;' should be used. This query accesses the LOGIN_HISTORY view in the ACCOUNT_USAGE schema, which contains the required login information.

q: What are common issues found by using the Query Profile? (Choose two.)
o: Identifying queries that will likely run very slowly before executing them
Locating queries that consume a high amount of credits
Identifying logical issues with the queries
Data spilling to a local or remote disk
e: Common issues identified by using the Query Profile in Snowflake include 'Identifying inefficient micro-partition pruning' and 'Data spilling to a local or remote disk'. These insights help in optimizing query performance by addressing data storage and processing inefficiencies.

q: The Snowflake Search Optimization Services supports improved performance of which kind of query?
o: Queries against large tables where frequent DML occurs
Queries against tables larger than 1 TB
Queries against a subset of columns in a table
e: The Snowflake Search Optimization Service is designed to enhance the performance of selective point lookup queries. These are queries that involve searching for a specific set of rows, typically using a WHERE clause with equality conditions on one or more columns.

q: Which file formats are supported for unloading data from Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake supports unloading data to Delimited (CSV, TSV, etc.) and JSON formats (and also Parquet). Avro is supported for loading, not unloading.

q: Which Snowflake tool would be BEST to troubleshoot network connectivity?
e: SnowCD (Snowflake Connectivity Diagnostic) is the tool designed specifically to troubleshoot network connectivity issues between Snowflake and client applications. It helps diagnose and resolve potential connection problems.

q: Increasing the size of a virtual warehouse from an X-Small to an X-Large is an example of which of the following?
e: Increasing the size of a virtual warehouse from X-Small to X-Large in Snowflake is an example of 'scaling up'. Scaling up involves increasing the compute resources (like CPU, memory) available to a single warehouse to enhance its processing capabilities.

q: What are ways to create and manage data shares in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: Using the CREATE SHARE AS SELECT * FROM TABLE command
e: Data shares in Snowflake can be created and managed through the Snowflake web interface (UI) and through SQL commands. These methods allow users to share data securely and efficiently with other Snowflake accounts or consumer accounts.

q: What is a characteristic of data micro-partitioning in Snowflake?
o: Micro-partitioning requires the definition of a partitioning schema
Micro-partitioning happens when the data is loaded
Micro-partitioning can be disabled within a Snowflake account
e: A key characteristic of data micro-partitioning in Snowflake is that it occurs automatically when data is loaded into the system. Snowflake handles micro-partitioning internally, optimizing data storage and access without requiring user intervention for partition schema definition.

q: Users with the ACCOUNTADMIN role can execute which of the following commands on existing users?
o: Can SHOW users DESCRIBE a given user, or ALTER or DROP a user
Can DEFINE users, DESCRIBE a given user, or ALTER or DELETE a user
Can SHOW users, INDEX a given user, or ALTER or DELETE a user
Can SHOW users, DEFINE a given user or ALTER, DROP, or MODIFY a user
e: Users with the ACCOUNTADMIN role have the ability to 'SHOW' users, 'DESCRIBE' a given user, and 'ALTER' or 'DROP' a user. This role grants the highest level of privileges in Snowflake, including comprehensive user and role management capabilities.

q: According to Snowflake best practice recommendations, which system-defined roles should be used to create custom roles? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake best practice recommends using USERADMIN to manage users and roles and SYSADMIN as the system role at the top of the custom-role hierarchy for owning/managing objects. SECURITYADMIN is primarily for granting/revoking privileges.

q: What services are provided by the cloud services layer in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: The cloud services layer in Snowflake provides 'Metadata management' and 'Authentication' services. This layer is responsible for managing all metadata operations and ensuring secure access to Snowflake accounts and objects.

q: Which of the following commands are valid options for the VALIDATION_MODE parameter within the Snowflake COPY_INTO command? (Choose two.)
e: For the VALIDATION_MODE parameter in the Snowflake COPY_INTO command, the valid options include 'RETURN_ALL_ERRORS' and 'RETURN_N_ERRORS'. These options control how Snowflake handles and reports errors encountered during the data loading process.

q: Snowflake virtual warehouses are part of which layer of the Snowflake architecture?
e: In the Snowflake architecture, virtual warehouses are part of the Compute layer. This layer is responsible for executing all data processing tasks, such as queries and data manipulation, separate from the Storage layer where data is stored.

q: Which of the following are characteristics of schemas used in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
o: A schema may contain one or more databases.
A database may contain one or more schemas.
A schema represents a logical grouping of database objects.
Each schema is contained within a virtual warehouse.
A table can span more than one schema.
e: In Snowflake, a schema is a logical grouping of database objects like tables, views, and functions, and each database may contain one or more schemas. Schemas help in organizing these objects within a database.

q: Which Snowflake objects can be used to reduce data storage costs for short-lived tables? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, Temporary tables and Transient tables can be used to reduce data storage costs for short-lived tables. Temporary tables are session-specific and are automatically dropped at the end of a session, while Transient tables are more durable but have reduced storage costs compared to permanent tables.

q: A user has unloaded data from Snowflake to a stage. Which SQL command should be used to validate which data was loaded into the stage?
e: The 'list @file_stage' SQL command is used in Snowflake to validate which files are present in a stage after unloading data. This command provides a list of files in the specified stage.

q: What are benefits of using the ACCESS_HISTORY view in the SNOWFLAKE database?
o: Identification of which roles have been used
Highlighting of row access policy usage
Identification of who has read data
e: ACCESS_HISTORY is used to discover unused data and to audit access/write activity. The documented benefit relevant to the options is identification of unused data; the docs do not state a benefit of identifying who has read data.

q: Which of the following view types are available in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, the available view types include 'Secure view' and 'Materialized view'. Secure views provide controlled access to sensitive data, while materialized views store precomputed results of a query for performance optimization.

q: Which of the following statements describes a benefit of Snowflake’s separation of compute and storage? (Choose two.)
o: Growth of storage and compute are tightly coupled.
Storage expands without the requirement to add more compute.
Compute can be scaled up or down without the requirement to add more storage.
Compute and storage can be scaled together.
Use of storage avoids disk spilling.
e: The benefits of Snowflake’s separation of compute and storage include the ability to expand storage without adding more compute resources, and the flexibility to scale compute up or down independently of storage. This architecture provides scalability and cost-effectiveness.

q: Which of the following languages can be used to implement Snowflake User Defined Functions (UDFs)? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, User Defined Functions (UDFs) can be implemented using 'Javascript' and 'SQL'. These languages provide the necessary capabilities to create custom functions for various data processing and analytical tasks.

q: What is the default compression type when unloading data from Snowflake?
e: When unloading data from Snowflake, the default compression type is 'gzip'. This widely-used compression format balances compression ratio and speed, providing efficient data unloading and transfer.

q: Which statement describes when a virtual warehouse can be resized?
o: A resize will affect running, queued, and new queries.
A resize can only be completed when the warehouse is in an auto-resume status.
A resize must be completed when the warehouse is suspended.
A resize can be completed at any time.
e: In Snowflake, a virtual warehouse can be resized at any time. This flexibility allows users to adjust the compute resources of a warehouse dynamically, according to the current workload and performance requirements.

q: What is the compressed size limit for semi-structured data loaded into a VARIANT data type using the COPY command?
e: The compressed size limit for semi-structured data loaded into a VARIANT data type using the COPY command in Snowflake is 16 MB. This limit ensures efficient processing and querying of semi-structured data within Snowflake.

q: User A cloned a schema and overwrote a schema that User B was working on. User B no longer has access to their version of the tables. However, this all occurred within the Time Travel retention period defined at the database level. How should the missing tables be restored?
o: Use a CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement
Rename the cloned schema and use an UNDROP SCHEMA statement.
Contact Snowflake Support to retrieve the data from Fail-safe
e: If User B's tables were overwritten within the Time Travel retention period, they can be restored using the 'UNDROP TABLE' statement. This command will recover the dropped tables from the Time Travel history, provided it is within the retention period.

q: How does Snowflake recommend handling the bulk loading of data batches from files already available in cloud storage?
e: For the bulk loading of data batches from files already available in cloud storage, Snowflake recommends using the COPY command. This command is optimized for loading large volumes of data efficiently and supports various file formats.

q: What is Snowflake's general guideline for files used to load data?
o: Files can be loaded directly into a table.
Any delimiter is supported: the default is a semicolon.
Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) is one of the supported semi-structured formats.
For delimited files, the default character set is UTF-8.
e: Snowflake's general guideline for loading data from files, particularly delimited files, is that the default character set is UTF-8. This encoding supports a wide range of characters and is commonly used for text data.

q: How does a Snowflake user execute an anonymous block of code?
o: The user must run the CALL command to execute the block.
The statements that define the block must also execute the block.
The SUBMIT command must run immediately after the block is defined
The block must be saved to a worksheet and executed using a connector.
e: In Snowflake, an anonymous block of code is executed by the statements that define the block itself. This means that when the block is defined in a script or query window, it is also executed immediately without the need for a separate command.

q: When unloading data from Snowflake, the user executes a COPY INTO command into an internal stage. What additional command is required to load the file onto the local file system?
e: After unloading data to an internal stage using the COPY INTO command, the 'GET' command is used to download the files from the stage to the local file system. This enables users to export data from Snowflake to their local environment.

q: A Snowflake user has a query that is running for a long time. When the user opens the query profiler, it indicates that a lot of data is spilling to disk. What is causing this to happen?
o: The result cache is almost full and is unable to hold the results.
The cloud storage staging area is not sufficient to hold the data results.
Clustering has not been applied to the table so the table is not optimized.
The warehouse memory is not sufficient to hold the intermediate query results.
e: When a query in Snowflake spills data to disk, it usually indicates that the memory allocated to the warehouse is not sufficient to hold all the intermediate results of the query. Increasing the size of the warehouse can help reduce or eliminate data spilling to disk.

q: What is the MOST performant file format for loading data in Snowflake?
e: Parquet is a columnar storage file format and is generally the most performant for loading data in Snowflake. It allows for efficient compression and encoding schemes, which can reduce the amount of data scanned and speed up query performance.

q: Which chart type does Snowsight support to visualize worksheet data?
e: Según la documentación oficial de Snowflake, Snowsight soporta únicamente los siguientes tipos de gráficos: Bar charts (Gráficos de barras), Line charts (Gráficos de líneas), Scatterplots (Gráficos de dispersión), Heat grids (Cuadrículas de calor), y Scorecards (Tarjetas de puntuación). De las opciones presentadas, únicamente Scatterplot está soportado. Box plot, Bubble chart y Pie chart NO están soportados por Snowsight.

q: Which result shows efficient pruning?
o: Partitions scanned is greater than partitions total.
Partitions scanned is less than partitions total.
Partitions scanned is equal to the partitions total.
Partitions scanned is greater than or equal to the partitions total.
e: Efficient pruning is indicated when the number of partitions scanned is less than the total number of partitions. This means that Snowflake is effectively using the partitioning information to skip over irrelevant partitions, thereby reducing the amount of data scanned and improving query performance.

q: Which clustering indicator will show if a large table in Snowflake will benefit from explicitly defining a clustering key?
e: The 'Depth' clustering indicator is used in Snowflake to show if a large table will benefit from explicitly defining a clustering key. A high depth value indicates unevenly distributed data across the micro-partitions, which can be optimized by defining a clustering key.

q: Which file format is MOST performant in Snowflake for data loading?
e: Snowflake’s documentation does not identify CSV as the most performant load format. CSV is simply the default delimited format, with a specific optimization for some large uncompressed files. Among the given choices, Parquet is the best-supported answer for high-performance loading.

q: What is to be expected when sharing worksheets in Snowsight?
o: Worksheets can be shared with users that are internal or external to any organization.
To run a shared worksheet, a user must be granted the role used for the worksheet session context.
Snowsight allows users to view and refresh results but not to edit shared worksheets.
Snowsight offers different sharing permissions at the worksheet, folder, and dashboard level.
e: When a worksheet is shared in Snowsight, recipients can edit or view it depending on permissions, and to run it they must have the worksheet’s role/session context.

q: Which Snowflake objects track DML changes made to tables, like inserts, updates, and deletes?
e: In Snowflake, 'Streams' are the objects that track DML (Data Manipulation Language) changes made to tables, such as inserts, updates, and deletes. Streams capture changes to a table since the last time a stream was consumed, providing a powerful mechanism for change data capture.

q: Which table type is automatically deleted after a session is closed and has no Fail-safe or Time Travel cost?
e: Temporary tables in Snowflake are automatically deleted after a session is closed and do not incur Fail-safe or Time Travel costs. These tables are session-specific and are ideal for transient data needs where long-term storage is not required.

q: Which constraint type is enforced in Snowflake from the ANSI SQL standard?
e: In Snowflake, the 'NOT NULL' constraint is enforced as per the ANSI SQL standard. This constraint ensures that a column cannot contain null values. Other constraints like UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, and FOREIGN KEY are recognized but not enforced in Snowflake.

q: Which function is used to profile warehouse credit usage?
e: The 'WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY' function is used to profile warehouse credit usage in Snowflake. This function provides historical data about the credits consumed by each virtual warehouse, which is useful for understanding and managing costs.

q: What is a characteristic of the Snowflake query profiler?
o: It can provide statistics on a maximum number of 100 queries per week.
It provides a graphic representation of the main components of the query processing.
It provides detailed statistics about which queries are using the greatest number of compute resources.
It can be used by third-party software using the query profiler API.
e: One key characteristic of the Snowflake query profiler is that it provides a graphic representation of the main components of the query processing. This graphical interface helps users understand and optimize their query performance by visually displaying the different stages and resources involved in query execution.

q: A Snowflake user wants to share transactional data with retail suppliers. However, some of the suppliers do not use Snowflake. According to best practice, what should the Snowflake user do? (Choose two.)
o: Provide each non-Snowflake supplier with their own reader account.
Deploy a single reader account to be shared by all of the non-Snowflake suppliers.
Create an ETL pipeline that uses select and inserts statements from the source to the target supplier accounts.
Use a data share for suppliers in the same cloud region and a replicated proxy share for other cloud deployments.
Extract the shared transactional data to an external stage and use cloud storage utilities to reload the suppliers' regions.
e: Best practices for sharing data with non-Snowflake users include providing each non-Snowflake supplier with their own reader account, which allows them access to a Snowflake account for querying shared data. Alternatively, Snowflake data providers can share data with data consumers in a different region.

q: Which statement about data sharing is true?
o: Accounts can share with other accounts regardless of their Snowflake edition, without requiring help from Snowflake Support.
Data sharing can cross regions, but not cloud providers.
The Data Consumer can only see objects in the Data Provider’s source database that have been explicitly added to the share.
A Data Provider can only share with other Snowflake customers.
e: In Snowflake data sharing, the data consumer can only access objects in the data provider's source database that have been explicitly added to the share. This ensures that the data provider has full control over what data is shared and who has access to it.

q: Which command is used to load files into an internal stage within Snowflake?
e: The 'COPY INTO' command in Snowflake is used to load files into an internal stage. This command reads data from files in a staged location and loads it into a Snowflake table. The 'PUT' command is used to upload files to a stage, but the actual loading into tables is performed by 'COPY INTO'.

q: Which object type is granted permissions for reading a table?
e: In Snowflake, permissions for reading a table are granted to a 'Role'. Roles are used to manage access and privileges within Snowflake, allowing users who are assigned these roles to perform actions such as reading tables.

q: What is the default value in the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) for auto suspending a Virtual Warehouse?
e: The default value for auto suspending a Virtual Warehouse in the Snowflake Web Interface (UI) is '10 minutes'. This setting determines how long a warehouse remains idle before it is automatically suspended to save on compute resources.

q: Several users are using the same virtual warehouse. The users report that the queries are running slowly, and that many queries are being queued. What is the recommended way to resolve this issue?
o: Reduce the warehouse STATEMENT_QUEUED_TIMEOUT_IN SECONDS parameter.
e: To resolve the issue of slow query performance and queuing in a shared virtual warehouse, it is recommended to increase the 'MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT' parameter. This will allow the warehouse to scale out and handle more concurrent queries, thereby reducing queuing and improving query performance.

q: Which data types are valid in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: The 'Variant' data type can store semi-structured data such as JSON, Avro, ORC, Parquet, or XML. 'Geography' is a geospatial data type.

q: What happens when the size of a virtual warehouse is changed?
o: Queries that are running on the current warehouse configuration are not impacted.
Queries that are running on the current warehouse configuration are aborted and have to be resubmitted by the user.
Queries that are running on the current warehouse configuration are aborted and are automatically resubmitted.
Queries that are running on the current warehouse configuration are moved to the new configuration and finished there.
e: When the size of a virtual warehouse in Snowflake is changed, queries that are currently running on the warehouse are not impacted. They will continue to run using the original warehouse configuration until completion. Any new queries submitted after the change will use the new warehouse configuration.

q: How often are encryption keys automatically rotated by Snowflake?
e: All Snowflake-managed keys are automatically rotated by Snowflake when they are more than 30 days old.

q: As a best practice, all custom roles should be granted to which system-defined role?
e: Instead, we recommend creating a hierarchy of roles aligned with business functions in your organization and ultimately assigning these roles to the SYSADMIN role. For more information, see Aligning Object Access with Business Functions in this topic.

q: Which Snowflake object can be accessed in the FROM clause of a query, returning a set of rows having one or more columns?
e: In Snowflake, a User-Defined Table Function (UDTF) can be accessed in the FROM clause of a query. UDTFs return a set of rows with one or more columns, making them suitable for use in such queries.

q: How are micro-partitions typically generated in Snowflake?
e: In Snowflake, micro-partitions are generated automatically. As data is loaded into a table, Snowflake automatically divides the data into micro-partitions based on the size and structure of the incoming data. This process is managed internally by Snowflake and requires no explicit action from the user.

q: What does Snowflake recommend regarding database object ownership? (Choose two.)
o: Create objects with ACCOUNTADMIN and do not reassign ownership.
Create objects with SECURITYADMIN to ease granting of privileges later.
Create objects with a custom role and grant this role to SYSADMIN.
Use only managed access schemas for objects owned by ACCOUNTADMIN.
e: Snowflake recommends creating objects with a custom role and granting this role to SYSADMIN for better access control and organization. Also, using only managed access schemas for objects owned by ACCOUNTADMIN helps maintain security and proper access permissions.

q: Other than ownership what privileges does a user need to view and modify resource monitors in Snowflake? (Choose two.)
e: To view and modify resource monitors in Snowflake, a user needs 'MONITOR' privileges to view the resource monitor and 'MODIFY' privileges to modify it. These privileges allow the user to manage and adjust resource monitors effectively.

q: What technique does Snowflake recommend for determining which virtual warehouse size to select?
o: Always start with an X-Small and increase the size if the query does not complete in 2 minutes
Experiment by running the same queries against warehouses of different sizes
Use the default size Snowflake chooses
Use X-Large or above for tables larger than 1 GB
e: Snowflake recommends experimenting by running the same queries against warehouses of different sizes to determine the most efficient size for a particular workload. This approach allows users to balance performance and cost by finding the warehouse size that best fits their specific use case.

q: Which command should be used when loading many flat files into a single table?
e: When loading many flat files into a single table, the 'COPY INTO' command is the most efficient choice in Snowflake. This command allows for bulk loading of data from files into a table, optimizing the data loading process.

q: How can a Snowflake user share data with another user who does not have a Snowflake account?
o: Share the data by implementing User-Defined Functions (UDFs)
Create a reader account and create a share of the data
Grant the READER privilege to the database that is going to be shared
Move the Snowflake account to a region where data sharing is enabled
e: To share data with a user who does not have a Snowflake account, the best approach is to create a reader account and then create a share of the data. This enables external users to access the shared data through the reader account without needing a Snowflake account of their own.

q: Which semi-structured data formats can be loaded into Snowflake with a COPY command? (Choose two.)
e: Snowflake supports loading semi-structured data formats using the COPY command. Among the given options, ORC and XML are the semi-structured data formats that can be loaded into Snowflake. CSV, while supported, is not considered a semi-structured format, and EDI and HTML are not directly supported for loading via COPY command.

q: Which statements reflect valid commands when using secondary roles? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, 'USE SECONDARY ROLES ALL' and 'USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE' are valid commands when managing secondary roles. 'USE SECONDARY ROLES ALL' enables all secondary roles granted to the user, while 'USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE' disables all secondary roles.

q: How long is a query visible in the Query History page in the Snowflake Web Interface (UI)?
e: In the Snowflake Web Interface (UI), the Query History page retains and displays queries for up to 14 days. This allows users to review and analyze queries executed within this period.

q: Two users share a virtual warehouse named WH_DEV_01. When one of the users loads data, the other one experiences performance issues while querying data. How does Snowflake recommend resolving this issue?
o: Create separate warehouses for each user
Create separate warehouses for each workload
Stop loading and querying data at the same time
e: Snowflake recommends creating separate virtual warehouses for different workloads to resolve performance issues. By separating the workloads (data loading and querying) into different warehouses, each user can operate without impacting the performance of the other.

q: What is a feature of a stored procedure in Snowflake?
o: They can be created as secure and hide the underlying metadata from all users.
They can only access tables from a single database.
They can only contain a single SQL statement.
They can be created to run with a caller's rights or an owner's rights.
e: A feature of stored procedures in Snowflake is that they can be created to run with either the caller's rights or the owner's rights. This allows control over the execution context of the stored procedure, determining whether it executes with the privileges of the user who calls it or the user who created it.

q: Which view will return users who have queried a table?
e: The view 'SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY' in Snowflake provides information about the access history of objects within Snowflake, including details on which users have queried a table. This view is useful for auditing and monitoring purposes.

q: Why do Snowflake’s virtual warehouses have scaling policies?
o: To help save extra storage costs
To help increase the performance of serverless computing features
To help control the credits consumed by a multi-cluster warehouse running in auto-scale mode
To help control the credits consumed by a multi-cluster warehouse running in maximized mode
e: Snowflake's virtual warehouses have scaling policies, particularly to control the credits consumed by a multi-cluster warehouse running in auto-scale mode. This ensures efficient resource usage and cost management while maintaining performance.

q: Where can a Snowflake user find the query history in Snowsight?
e: In Snowsight, Snowflake's user interface, the query history can be found under the 'Activity' section. This area provides a detailed history of the queries executed, including their status, duration, and other relevant information.

q: What is SnowSQL?
o: Snowflake's new user interface where users can visualize data into charts and dashboards.
Snowflake's proprietary extension of the ANSI SQL standard, including built-in keywords and system functions.
Snowflake's command line client built on the Python connector which is used to connect to Snowflake and execute SQL.
Snowflake's library that provides a programming interface for processing data on Snowflake without moving it to the system where the application code runs.
e: SnowSQL is Snowflake's command line client, which is built on the Python connector. It is used to connect to Snowflake and execute SQL commands. SnowSQL offers a text-based interface for interacting with Snowflake, managing objects, and running queries.

To determine the output of the last select statement, the specific SQL statements that were executed prior to it are required. Without knowing these statements, it is not possible to accurately predict the output of the select statement.

q: Which statement is true of zero-copy cloning?
o: It increases storage costs as cloning a table requires storing its data twice
A cloned table includes the load history of the original source
It is licensed as an additional Snowflake feature
All micro-partitions between the original and cloned tables are fully shared
e: Zero-copy cloning in Snowflake means that all micro-partitions between the original and cloned tables are fully shared. This approach does not require additional storage for the cloned data, as it leverages Snowflake's unique architecture to reference the same underlying data without duplicating it.

q: A Snowflake user has been granted the CREATE DATA EXCHANGE LISTING privilege with their role. Which tasks can this user now perform on the Data Exchange? (Choose two.)
e: With the CREATE DATA EXCHANGE LISTING privilege, a Snowflake user can modify listings properties and submit listings for approval or publishing on the Data Exchange. This allows them to manage and promote their data listings effectively within the Snowflake Data Exchange.

q: Which parameter prevents streams on tables from becoming stale?
e: The MAX_DATA_EXTENSION_TIME_IN_DAYS parameter prevents streams on tables from becoming stale by extending the data retention period for the source table beyond the default DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS. This ensures the stream's offset does not expire before the data is consumed. STALE_AFTER is a read-only stream property that indicates when the stream will become stale, not a parameter that prevents staleness. MIN_DATA_RETENSION_TIME_IN_DAYS is not a valid Snowflake parameter.

q: If a virtual warehouse runs for 30 seconds after it is provisioned, how many seconds will the customer be billed for?
e: In Snowflake, the billing for virtual warehouse usage is done on a per-second basis, with a minimum of 60 seconds. So, even if a warehouse runs for only 30 seconds, the customer will be billed for a full 60 seconds as that is the minimum billable time unit.

q: When should a stored procedure be created with caller's rights?
o: When the caller needs to be prevented from viewing the source code of the stored procedure
When the caller needs to run a statement that could not execute outside of the stored procedure
When the stored procedure needs to run with the privileges of the role that called the stored procedure
When the stored procedure needs to operate on objects that the caller does not have privileges on
e: A stored procedure should be created with caller's rights when it needs to run with the privileges of the role that called the stored procedure. This approach ensures that the procedure operates within the security and access constraints of the calling user, respecting their permissions and privileges.

q: What JavaScript delimiters are available in Snowflake stored procedures? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake stored procedures written in JavaScript, two body delimiters are available: the double dollar sign ($$) and the single quote ('). The double dollar sign is recommended because it avoids escaping issues when the JavaScript code contains embedded single quotes. Double forward slashes (//) are comment delimiters in JavaScript, not procedure body delimiters.

q: What type of function can be used to estimate the approximate number of distinct values from a table that has trillions of rows?
e: The HyperLogLog (HLL) function in Snowflake can be used to estimate the approximate number of distinct values in a very large dataset, such as a table with trillions of rows. HLL is an algorithm designed for efficient approximation of the count of distinct values.

q: Which Data Definition Language (DDL) commands are supported by Snowflake to manage tags? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, the 'ALTER TAG' and 'DROP TAG' commands are supported as Data Definition Language (DDL) commands to manage tags. These commands allow users to modify and delete tags, respectively, for managing metadata associated with Snowflake objects.

q: What Snowflake objects can be added to a share? (Choose two.)
e: In Snowflake, both 'Tables' and 'Secure views' can be added to a share. These objects can be shared with other Snowflake accounts or with external entities through reader accounts, facilitating data sharing and collaboration.

q: A Query Profile shows a UnionAll operator with an extra Aggregate operator on top. What does this signify?
o: Queries that are too large to fit in memory
e: In a Snowflake Query Profile, if a UnionAll operator is shown with an extra Aggregate operator on top, it typically signifies the use of 'UNION' without the 'ALL' keyword. This extra Aggregate operator is used to remove duplicates, which is the default behavior of the UNION operator.

q: Which data governance control has Snowflake embedded in the application?
e: Snowflake has embedded 'Attribute-based access control' as a data governance control in the application. This control allows fine-grained access permissions based on attributes like user roles, data tags, and more, enabling organizations to implement robust data governance policies.

q: What actions does the use of the PUT command do automatically? (Choose two.)
o: It creates a file format object.
It uses the last stage created.
It compresses all files using GZIP.
It encrypts the file data in transit.
It creates an empty target table.
e: The PUT command in Snowflake automatically compresses files using GZIP and encrypts the file data in transit. These actions optimize file transfer to stages and enhance security, respectively.

q: Which command should a Snowflake user execute to load data into a table?
e: To load data into a table in Snowflake, the user should execute the command 'copy into mytable from @my_int_stage;'. This command specifies the table and the stage (location of files) from which to load the data.

q: Which function returns the URL of a stage using the stage name as the input?
e: The 'GET_STAGE_LOCATION' function in Snowflake returns the URL of a stage, given the stage name as input. This function is useful for retrieving the location of a specific stage in Snowflake.

q: What is the MAXIMUM number of clusters that can be provisioned with a multi-cluster virtual warehouse? D. 100
e: A multi-cluster warehouse must have a maximum cluster count greater than 1. In Snowsight, the highest Max Clusters value you can select is 10, and the SQL maximum varies by warehouse size. Among the provided options, 10 is the correct choice.

q: Which Snowflake table supports unstructured data?
e:
- Directory: Las Directory Tables (tablas de directorio) son el mecanismo de Snowflake para gestionar datos no estructurados. Se asocian a stages internos o externos y proporcionan un catalogo de los archivos almacenados (imagenes, PDFs, videos, etc.), incluyendo URLs para acceder a ellos.
- Transient: Las tablas transitorias almacenan datos estructurados/semi-estructurados temporales. No estan disenadas para datos no estructurados.
- Temporary: Las tablas temporales existen solo durante la sesion del usuario. No soportan datos no estructurados.
- Permanent: Las tablas permanentes almacenan datos estructurados y semi-estructurados (VARIANT), pero no datos no estructurados como archivos binarios.

q: When unloading data, which file format preserves the data values for floating-point number columns?
e: The Parquet file format is the most effective for preserving the data values of floating-point number columns when unloading data from Snowflake. Parquet is a columnar storage format that efficiently handles different data types, including floating-point numbers, with high fidelity.

q: Which virtual warehouse privilege is required to view a load-monitoring chart?
e: To view a load-monitoring chart of a virtual warehouse in Snowflake, the 'MONITOR' privilege is required. This privilege allows users to observe and assess the performance and usage of the virtual warehouse.

q: Which use case will always cause an exploding join in Snowflake?
o: A query that has more than 10 left outer joins.
A query that is using a UNION without an ALL.
A query that has not specified join criteria for tables.
A query that has requested too many columns of data.
e: An exploding join in Snowflake typically occurs when a query does not specify join criteria for tables. This lack of criteria can lead to a Cartesian product, where each row of one table is joined to every row of another, causing an exponential increase in the number of rows returned.

q: How many resource monitors can be applied to a single virtual warehouse?
e: In Snowflake, only one resource monitor can be applied to a single virtual warehouse at a time. This monitor is used to track and control the credits consumed by the warehouse, ensuring efficient and cost-effective operation.

q: What are the main differences between the account usage views and the information schema views? (Choose two.)
o: No active warehouse is needed to query account usage views but one is needed to query information schema views.
Account usage views do not contain data about tables but information schema views do.
Account usage views contain dropped objects but information schema views do not.
Data retention for account usage views is 1 year but is 7 days to 6 months for information schema views, depending on the view.
Information schema views are read-only but account usage views are not.
e: The main differences between account usage views and information schema views in Snowflake are that account usage views contain data about dropped objects, which information schema views do not, and account usage views have a data retention period of 1 year, while information schema views retain data for a period ranging from 7 days to 6 months, depending on the specific view.

q: Which file function provides a URL with access to a file on a stage without the need for authentication and authorization?
e: The 'GET_PRESIGNED_URL' function in Snowflake provides a URL with access to a file on a stage without the need for authentication and authorization. This function generates a presigned URL that grants temporary access to the file, simplifying the process of file sharing and access.

q: Which view can be used to determine if a table has frequent row updates or deletes?
e: The 'TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS' view in Snowflake can be used to determine if a table has frequent row updates or deletes. This view provides metrics related to the storage utilization of tables, including information on micro-partition changes that can indicate frequent updates or deletions.

q: How does the Snowflake search optimization service improve query performance?
o: It improves the performance of range searches.
It defines different clustering keys on the same source table.
It improves the performance of all queries running against a given table.
It improves the performance of equality searches.
e: The Snowflake search optimization service primarily improves the performance of range searches. By optimizing how data is stored and accessed, it reduces the time and resources needed to execute range queries, leading to faster query performance.

q: How is unstructured data retrieved from data storage?
o: SQL functions like the GET command can be used to copy the unstructured data to a location on the client.
SQL functions can be used to create different types of URLs pointing to the unstructured data. These URLs can be used to download the data to a client.
SQL functions can be used to retrieve the data from the query results cache. When the query results are output to a client, the unstructured data will be output to the client as files.
SQL functions can call on different web extensions designed to display different types of files as a web page. The web extensions will allow the files to be downloaded to the client.
e: In Snowflake, SQL functions can be used to create different types of URLs that point to unstructured data stored in stages. These URLs can then be used by clients to download the data directly. This approach allows easy and direct access to unstructured data without the need for complex retrieval mechanisms.

q: What is the recommended way to obtain a cloned table with the same grants as the source table?
o: Clone the table with the COPY GRANTS command.
Use an ALTER TABLE command to copy the grants.
Clone the schema then drop the unwanted tables.
Create a script to extract grants and apply them to the cloned table.
e: The recommended way to obtain a cloned table with the same grants as the source table in Snowflake is to use the 'COPY GRANTS' option. When cloning a table with this option, all grants on the source table are also applied to the cloned table, preserving the access permissions.

q: What common query issues can be identified using the Query Profile? (Choose two.)
e: Using the Query Profile in Snowflake, common query issues such as 'exploding joins' and 'inefficient pruning' can be identified. Exploding joins occur when the join criteria lead to a large increase in the number of rows returned. Inefficient pruning refers to cases where the query engine scans more data than necessary.

q: What is used to extract the content of PDF files stored in Snowflake stages?
e: To extract the content of PDF files stored in Snowflake stages, a Java User-Defined Function (UDF) can be used. Java UDFs allow the execution of custom Java code within Snowflake, which is suitable for processing complex data types like PDF.

q: What is used to extract the content of PDF files stored in Snowflake stages?
e: To extract the content of PDF files stored in Snowflake stages, a Java User-Defined Function (UDF) can be used. Java UDFs allow the execution of custom Java code within Snowflake, which is suitable for processing complex data types like PDF.

q: What happens when a database is cloned?
o: It does not retain any privileges granted on the source object.
It replicates all granted privileges on the corresponding source objects.
It replicates all granted privileges on the corresponding child objects.
It replicates all granted privileges on the corresponding child schema objects.
e: When a database is cloned in Snowflake, the clone inherits all granted privileges on the clones of the child objects contained in the source database. However, the database container itself does not inherit the privileges granted on the source container. In other words, grants on schemas, tables, views, and other contained objects are copied to the cloned objects, but the source database’s own privileges are not copied to the new database.

q: What does a Query Profile provide in Snowflake?
o: A multi-step query that displays each processing step in the same panel.
A pre-computed data set derived from a query specification and stored for later use.
A graphical representation of the main components of the processing plan for a query.
